verses.sa:
उतरि तुरग तें कीन्ह प्रनामा ।
परम चतुर न कहेउ निज नामा ॥
verses.tr:
utari turag teṃ kīnh pranāmā
param catur na kaheu nij nāmā

verses.sa:
भूपति तृषित बिलोकि तेहिं सरबरु दीन्ह देखाइ ।
मज्जन पान समेत हय कीन्ह नृपति हरषाइ ॥
verses.tr:
bhūpati tṛṣit biloki tehiṃ sarabaru dīnh dekhāi
majjan pān samet haya kīnh nṛpati haraṣāi
verses.head: दोहा

trans: As he wandered through the forest, he spied a hermitage where dwelt a king in disguise of a holy man. He had been despoiled of his kingdom by Pratepabhanu, and had left his army on the field of battle, knowing that his adversary’s star was in the ascendant and his own io _the decline. Too proud to meet the king, too much mortified to go home, nursing the rage in his heart, he like a beggar, though a prince, took up his abode in the wood in the garb of an anchorite. He at once recognized King Pratapa-bhenu as he drew near; but the latter was too tired to recognize him, and looking only at his dress took him to be a holy man, and alighting from his horse saluted him; he was, however, too astute to declare his name.
Seeing the king to be faint with thirst, he pointed out to him a fine pond, where he bathed and drank, both he and his horse, with much gladness.

sections.label: Doha 159
sections.name: निसा घोर गम्भीर बन पंथ न सुनहु सुजान

verses.sa:
गै श्रम सकल सुखी नृप भयऊ ।
निज आश्रम तापस लै गयऊ ॥
verses.tr:
gai śram sakal sukhī nṛp bhayaū
nij āśram tāpas lai gayaū
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
आसन दीन्ह अस्त रबि जानी ।
पुनि तापस बोलेउ मृदु बानी ॥
verses.tr:
āsan dīnh ast rabi jānī
puni tāpas boleu mṛdu bānī

verses.sa:
को तुम्ह कस बन फिरहु अकेलें ।
सुंदर जुबा जीव परहेलें ॥
verses.tr:
ko tumh kas ban phirahu akeleṃ
suṃdar jubā jīv paraheleṃ

verses.sa:
चक्रबर्ति के लच्छन तोरें ।
देखत दया लागि अति मोरें ॥
verses.tr:
cakrabarti ke lacchan toreṃ
dekhat dayā lāgi ati moreṃ

verses.sa:
नाम प्रतापभानु अवनीसा ।
तासु सचिव मैं सुनहु मुनीसा ॥
verses.tr:
nām pratāpabhānu avanīsā
tāsu saciv maiṃ sunahu munīsā

verses.sa:
फिरत अहेरें परेउँ भुलाई ।
बडे भाग देखउँ पद आई ॥
verses.tr:
phirat ahereṃ pareum̐ bhulāī
baḍe bhāg dekhaum̐ pad āī

verses.sa:
हम कहँ दुर्लभ दरस तुम्हारा ।
जानत हौं कछु भल होनिहारा ॥
verses.tr:
ham kaham̐ durlabh daras tumhārā
jānat hauṃ kachu bhal honihārā

verses.sa:
कह मुनि तात भयउ अँधियारा ।
जोजन सत्तरि नगरु तुम्हारा ॥
verses.tr:
kah muni tāt bhayau am̐dhiyārā
jojan sattari nagaru tumhārā

verses.sa:
निसा घोर गम्भीर बन पंथ न सुनहु सुजान ।
बसहु आजु अस जानि तुम्ह जाएहु होत बिहान ॥
verses.tr:
nisā ghor gambhīr ban paṃth na sunahu sujān
basahu āju as jāni tumh jāehu hot bihān
verses.head: दोहा

verses.sa:
तुलसी जसि भवतब्यता तैसी मिलइ सहाइ ।
आपुनु आवइ ताहि पहिं ताहि तहाँ लै जाइ ॥
verses.tr:
tulasī jasi bhavatabyatā taisī milai sahāi
āpunu āvai tāhi pahiṃ tāhi tahām̐ lai jāi

trans: All his weariness passed away and he was quite happy again. The hermit took him to his cell and, as the sun had now set, showed him where he might rest; but yet enquired of him in courteous tones,—‘Who may you be, and why, thus young and beautiful, do you risk your life by roaming alone in the forest? You have all the marks of a great sovereign, and at the sight of you I am quite moved.” ‘Know then, reverend sir, that I am the minister of King Pratapabhinu; in pursuit of the chase I have lost my way, and by great good fortune have been brought into your presence. To get a sight of you was no easy matter, and I am satisfied that something good is about to befall me.” Said the hermit, —“ My son, it is now dusk, and your city is seventy leagues away.
The night is dark, the forest dense, and the road not easy to find. Tarry then here for to-day and start tomorrow at dawn.” Says Tulsi—Fate is furthered in its

sections.label: Doha 160
sections.name: कपट बोरि बानी मृदुल बोलेउ जुगुति समेत

verses.sa:
भलेहिं नाथ आयसु धरि सीसा ।
बाँधि तुरग तरु बैठ महीसा ॥
verses.tr:
bhalehiṃ nāth āyasu dhari sīsā
bām̐dhi turag taru baiṭh mahīsā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
नृप बहु भाँती प्रसंसेउ ताही ।
चरन बंदी निज भाग्य सराही ॥
verses.tr:
nṛp bahu bhām̐tī prasaṃseu tāhī
caran baṃdī nij bhāgya sarāhī

verses.sa:
पुनि बोले मृदु गिरा सुहाई ।
जानि पिता प्रभु करउँ ढिठाई ॥
verses.tr:
puni bole mṛdu girā suhāī
jāni pitā prabhu karaum̐ ḍhiṭhāī

verses.sa:
मोहि मुनीस सुत सेवक जानी ।
नाथ नाम निज कहहु बखानी ॥
verses.tr:
mohi munīs sut sevak jānī
nāth nām nij kahahu bakhānī

verses.sa:
तेहि न जान नृप नृपहि सो जाना ।
भूप सुह्रद सो कपट सयाना ॥
verses.tr:
tehi na jān nṛp nṛpahi so jānā
bhūp suhrad so kapaṭ sayānā

verses.sa:
बैरी पुनि छत्री पुनि राजा ।
छल बल कीन्ह चहइ निज काजा ॥
verses.tr:
bairī puni chatrī puni rājā
chal bal kīnh cahai nij kājā

verses.sa:
समुझि राजसुख दुखित अराती ।
अवाँ अनल इव सुलगइ छाती ॥
verses.tr:
samujhi rājasukh dukhit arātī
avām̐ anal iv sulagai chātī

verses.sa:
सरल बचन नृप के सुनि काना ।
बयर सँभारि हृदयँ हरषाना ॥
verses.tr:
saral bacan nṛp ke suni kānā
bayar sam̐bhāri hṛdayam̐ haraṣānā

verses.sa:
कपट बोरि बानी मृदुल बोलेउ जुगुति समेत ।
नाम हमार भिखारि अब निर्धन रहित निकेति ॥
verses.tr:
kapaṭ bori bānī mṛdul boleu juguti samet
nām hamār bhikhāri ab nirdhan rahit niketi
verses.head: दोहा

trans: own way; either you go to meet it, or itself comes and carries you off.

‘Very well, my lord, I obey your command;” and so saying the king tied up his horse toa tree and came and sat down. With many flattering speeches he bowed at his feet, extolling his own good fortune, and at last in modest and winning terms put the question, —‘Regarding you, my lord, as a father, I make bold and beg of you to look upon meas your son and servant and to declare to me your name.” Now the king did not recognize him, but he recognized the king, and was as false and crafty as the king was honest: moreover, being an enemy,:and at the same time both a warrior by caste and of royal birth, he was bent on accomplishing his own ends, whether by fraud or by right. In his enmity he was grieved to see the King’s prosperity, and his heart within him burned as with the fire of a furnace; but on hearing the prince's ae words he controlled his resentment and was glad at eart,
And uttered yet another smooth but false and artful speech, —“ My name is now Bhikhari, a homeless beggar.”

sections.label: Doha 161
sections.name: अब लगि मोहि न मिलेउ कोउ मैं न जनावउँ काहु

verses.sa:
कह नृप जे बिग्यान निधाना ।
तुम्ह सारिखे गलित अभिमाना ॥
verses.tr:
kah nṛp je bigyān nidhānā
tumh sārikhe galit abhimānā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
सदा रहहि अपनपौ दुराएँ ।
सब बिधि कुसल कुबेष बनाएँ ॥
verses.tr:
sadā rahahi apanapau durāem̐
sab bidhi kusal kubeṣ banāem̐

verses.sa:
तेहि तें कहहि संत श्रुति टेरें ।
परम अकिंचन प्रिय हरि केरें ॥
verses.tr:
tehi teṃ kahahi saṃt śruti ṭereṃ
param akiṃcan priya hari kereṃ

verses.sa:
तुम्ह सम अधन भिखारि अगेहा ।
होत बिरंचि सिवहि संदेहा ॥
verses.tr:
tumh sam adhan bhikhāri agehā
hot biraṃci sivahi saṃdehā

verses.sa:
जोसि सोसि तव चरन नमामी ।
मो पर कृपा करिअ अब स्वामी ॥
verses.tr:
josi sosi tav caran namāmī
mo par kṛpā karia ab svāmī

verses.sa:
सहज प्रीति भूपति कै देखी ।
आपु बिषय बिस्वास बिसेषी ॥
verses.tr:
sahaj prīti bhūpati kai dekhī
āpu biṣaya bisvās biseṣī

verses.sa:
सब प्रकार राजहि अपनाई ।
बोलेउ अधिक सनेह जनाई ॥
verses.tr:
sab prakār rājahi apanāī
boleu adhik saneh janāī

verses.sa:
सुनु सतिभाउ कहउँ महिपाला ।
इहाँ बसत बीते बहु काला ॥
verses.tr:
sunu satibhāu kahaum̐ mahipālā
ihām̐ basat bīte bahu kālā

verses.sa:
अब लगि मोहि न मिलेउ कोउ मैं न जनावउँ काहु ।
लोकमान्यता अनल सम कर तप कानन दाहु ॥
verses.tr:
ab lagi mohi na mileu kou maiṃ na janāvaum̐ kāhu
lokamānyatā anal sam kar tap kānan dāhu
verses.head: दोहा

verses.sa:
तुलसी देखि सुबेषु भूलहिं मूढ़ न चतुर नर ।
सुंदर केकिहि पेखु बचन सुधा सम असन अहि ॥
verses.tr:
tulasī dekhi subeṣu bhūlahiṃ mūr̤h na catur nar
suṃdar kekihi pekhu bacan sudhā sam asan ahi

trans: Said the king,—‘ Philosophers like you, with whom all self-consciousness has been extinguished, ever conceal their own personality, and are in every way blessed, though their outer garb be wretched. Therefore the saints proclaim aloud in men’s ears that it is the poor whom Hari holds most dear. A poor and homeless beggar, such as you are, is an anxiety to Brahma and Siva: at all events, I prostrate myself at your feet and beg of you to grant me your grace.” When he saw the king’s simple affection he waxed all the more confident, and won him over in every way, using words with a still greater show of friendliness, —‘Hearken, O king, while I relate the truth of the matter. I have for a long time dwelt here,
And till now neither has any one come to me, nor have [ spoken to any one; for worldly honour ia like a fire, and penance a forest for it to consume.”
Says Tulsi:—Fools are deceived by fair appearances, but not wise men: though a peacock is fair to look upon and its voice is pleasant,” yet it devours the saake.

sections.label: Doha 162
sections.name: आदिसृष्टि उपजी जबहिं तब उतपति भै मोरि

verses.sa:
तातें गुपुत रहउँ जग माहीं ।
हरि तजि किमपि प्रयोजन नाहीं ॥
verses.tr:
tāteṃ guput rahaum̐ jag māhīṃ
hari taji kimapi prayojan nāhīṃ
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
प्रभु जानत सब बिनहिं जनाएँ ।
कहहु कवनि सिधि लोक रिझाएँ ॥
verses.tr:
prabhu jānat sab binahiṃ janāem̐
kahahu kavani sidhi lok rijhāem̐

verses.sa:
तुम्ह सुचि सुमति परम प्रिय मोरें ।
प्रीति प्रतीति मोहि पर तोरें ॥
verses.tr:
tumh suci sumati param priya moreṃ
prīti pratīti mohi par toreṃ

verses.sa:
अब जौं तात दुरावउँ तोही ।
दारुन दोष घटइ अति मोही ॥
verses.tr:
ab jauṃ tāt durāvaum̐ tohī
dārun doṣ ghaṭai ati mohī

verses.sa:
जिमि जिमि तापसु कथइ उदासा ।
तिमि तिमि नृपहि उपज बिस्वासा ॥
verses.tr:
jimi jimi tāpasu kathai udāsā
timi timi nṛpahi upaj bisvāsā

verses.sa:
देखा स्वबस कर्म मन बानी ।
तब बोला तापस बगध्यानी ॥
verses.tr:
dekhā svabas karm man bānī
tab bolā tāpas bagadhyānī

verses.sa:
नाम हमार एकतनु भाई ।
सुनि नृप बोले पुनि सिरु नाई ॥
verses.tr:
nām hamār ekatanu bhāī
suni nṛp bole puni siru nāī

verses.sa:
कहहु नाम कर अरथ बखानी ।
मोहि सेवक अति आपन जानी ॥
verses.tr:
kahahu nām kar arath bakhānī
mohi sevak ati āpan jānī

verses.sa:
आदिसृष्टि उपजी जबहिं तब उतपति भै मोरि ।
नाम एकतनु हेतु तेहि देह न धरी बहोरि ॥
verses.tr:
ādisṛṣṭi upajī jabahiṃ tab utapati bhai mori
nām ekatanu hetu tehi deh na dharī bahori
verses.head: दोहा

trans: “Therefore I live retired in the world, and, save Hari, have no care whatever. The Lord knows everything without being told; so what isto be gained by conciliating the world But you are so good and sensible that I cannot but love you in return for the faith and confidence you have placed in me: and if I were to send you away, my son, it would be a very grievous sin on my part.” ‘The more the es i hermit talked of his detachment from the world, the more trustful grew the king; till at last the false anchorite, seeing him completely in his power, said,—“My name, brother, is Ektanu” (one body). The king bowed and asked further,—“Tell me, I pray, the meaning of this name, for surely I am your servant.”
“At the first dawn of creation my birth took place, and my name was Hktannu, for this reason that I have never taken any other body.

sections.label: Doha 163
sections.name: सुनु महीस असि नीति जहँ तहँ नाम न कहहिं नृप

verses.sa:
जनि आचरुज करहु मन माहीं ।
सुत तप तें दुर्लभ कछु नाहीं ॥
verses.tr:
jani ācaruj karahu man māhīṃ
sut tap teṃ durlabh kachu nāhīṃ
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
तपबल तें जग सृजइ बिधाता ।
तपबल बिष्नु भए परित्राता ॥
verses.tr:
tapabal teṃ jag sṛjai bidhātā
tapabal biṣnu bhae paritrātā

verses.sa:
तपबल संभु करहिं संघारा ।
तप तें अगम न कछु संसारा ॥
verses.tr:
tapabal saṃbhu karahiṃ saṃghārā
tap teṃ agam na kachu saṃsārā

verses.sa:
भयउ नृपहि सुनि अति अनुरागा ।
कथा पुरातन कहै सो लागा ॥
verses.tr:
bhayau nṛpahi suni ati anurāgā
kathā purātan kahai so lāgā

verses.sa:
करम धरम इतिहास अनेका ।
करइ निरूपन बिरति बिबेका ॥
verses.tr:
karam dharam itihās anekā
karai nirūpan birati bibekā

verses.sa:
उदभव पालन प्रलय कहानी ।
कहेसि अमित आचरज बखानी ॥
verses.tr:
udabhav pālan pralaya kahānī
kahesi amit ācaraj bakhānī

verses.sa:
सुनि महिप तापस बस भयऊ ।
आपन नाम कहत तब लयऊ ॥
verses.tr:
suni mahip tāpas bas bhayaū
āpan nām kahat tab layaū

verses.sa:
कह तापस नृप जानउँ तोही ।
कीन्हेहु कपट लाग भल मोही ॥
verses.tr:
kah tāpas nṛp jānaum̐ tohī
kīnhehu kapaṭ lāg bhal mohī

verses.sa:
सुनु महीस असि नीति जहँ तहँ नाम न कहहिं नृप ।
मोहि तोहि पर अति प्रीति सोइ चतुरता बिचारि तव ॥
verses.tr:
sunu mahīs asi nīti jaham̐ taham̐ nām na kahahiṃ nṛp
mohi tohi par ati prīti soi caturatā bicāri tav
verses.head: दोहा

trans: “Marvel not in your mind, my son; for nothing is too difficult for penance. By the power of penance the Creator created the world; by the power of penance Vishnu is the great redeemer; by the power of penance Siva works destruction; and to penance there is nothing in the world impossible.” The king, as he listened, was charmed, for he commenced relating old-world stories: many legends of pious deeds and holy lives; examples of asceticism and divine wisdom; tales of the birth, preservation, and destruction of the world, and innumerable other marvellous narratives. The king, ashe listened, yielded completely to his influence, and proceeded to tell him his true name. Said the hermit,—“O king, I knew you; though you tried to practise a trick upon me, took it quite in good part.
“Hear, O king; it is a political maxim!that on some occasions a king should not declare his name; and when I

sections.label: Doha 164
sections.name: जरा मरन दुख रहित तनु समर जितै जनि कोउ

verses.sa:
नाम तुम्हार प्रताप दिनेसा ।
सत्यकेतु तव पिता नरेसा ॥
verses.tr:
nām tumhār pratāp dinesā
satyaketu tav pitā naresā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
गुर प्रसाद सब जानिअ राजा ।
कहिअ न आपन जानि अकाजा ॥
verses.tr:
gur prasād sab jānia rājā
kahia na āpan jāni akājā

verses.sa:
देखि तात तव सहज सुधाई ।
प्रीति प्रतीति नीति निपुनाई ॥
verses.tr:
dekhi tāt tav sahaj sudhāī
prīti pratīti nīti nipunāī

verses.sa:
उपजि परि ममता मन मोरें ।
कहउँ कथा निज पूछे तोरें ॥
verses.tr:
upaji pari mamatā man moreṃ
kahaum̐ kathā nij pūche toreṃ

verses.sa:
अब प्रसन्न मैं संसय नाहीं ।
मागु जो भूप भाव मन माहीं ॥
verses.tr:
ab prasann maiṃ saṃsaya nāhīṃ
māgu jo bhūp bhāv man māhīṃ

verses.sa:
सुनि सुबचन भूपति हरषाना ।
गहि पद बिनय कीन्हि बिधि नाना ॥
verses.tr:
suni subacan bhūpati haraṣānā
gahi pad binaya kīnhi bidhi nānā

verses.sa:
कृपासिंधु मुनि दरसन तोरें ।
चारि पदारथ करतल मोरें ॥
verses.tr:
kṛpāsiṃdhu muni darasan toreṃ
cāri padārath karatal moreṃ

verses.sa:
प्रभुहि तथापि प्रसन्न बिलोकी ।
मागि अगम बर होउँ असोकी ॥
verses.tr:
prabhuhi tathāpi prasann bilokī
māgi agam bar houm̐ asokī

verses.sa:
जरा मरन दुख रहित तनु समर जितै जनि कोउ ।
एकछत्र रिपुहीन महि राज कलप सत होउ ॥
verses.tr:
jarā maran dukh rahit tanu samar jitai jani kou
ekachatr ripuhīn mahi rāj kalap sat hou
verses.head: दोहा

trans: observed your excellent sagacity I conceived a great affection for you.

“Your name is Pratapabhdou, and your father is king Satyaketu. sir, a spiritual man knows everything, there is no need of another's telling. Ah, my son, when I beheld your natural goodness, your faith and trustfulness, and your knowledge of state-craft, there sprung up an affection for youin my soul, and I told you my own story as you asked me. Now I am well pleased with you; doubt not, but ask whatever you will.” On hearing these fair words the king was delighted, and clasping his feet entreated him suppliantly,—‘ O merciful saint, by the sight of you the four objects of human desire have all come within my grasp. Yet, as I see my lord so gracious, I will ask an impossible boon and be happy for ever.
May I die of old age, free from bodily pain; may I never be conquered in battle: may earth rid of every foe be all under my sole sway, and may my empire last for a hundred ages.”

sections.label: Doha 165
sections.name: एवमस्तु कहि कपटमुनि बोला कुटिल बहोरि

verses.sa:
कह तापस नृप ऐसेइ होऊ ।
कारन एक कठिन सुनु सोऊ ॥
verses.tr:
kah tāpas nṛp aisei hoū
kāran ek kaṭhin sunu soū
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
कालउ तुअ पद नाइहि सीसा ।
एक बिप्रकुल छाड़ि महीसा ॥
verses.tr:
kālau tua pad nāihi sīsā
ek biprakul chār̤i mahīsā

verses.sa:
तपबल बिप्र सदा बरिआरा ।
तिन्ह के कोप न कोउ रखवारा ॥
verses.tr:
tapabal bipr sadā bariārā
tinh ke kop na kou rakhavārā

verses.sa:
जौं बिप्रन्ह सब करहु नरेसा ।
तौ तुअ बस बिधि बिष्नु महेसा ॥
verses.tr:
jauṃ bipranh sab karahu naresā
tau tua bas bidhi biṣnu mahesā

verses.sa:
चल न ब्रह्मकुल सन बरिआई ।
सत्य कहउँ दोउ भुजा उठाई ॥
verses.tr:
cal na brahmakul san bariāī
satya kahaum̐ dou bhujā uṭhāī

verses.sa:
बिप्र श्राप बिनु सुनु महिपाला ।
तोर नास नहि कवनेहुँ काला ॥
verses.tr:
bipr śrāp binu sunu mahipālā
tor nās nahi kavanehum̐ kālā

verses.sa:
हरषेउ राउ बचन सुनि तासू ।
नाथ न होइ मोर अब नासू ॥
verses.tr:
haraṣeu rāu bacan suni tāsū
nāth na hoi mor ab nāsū

verses.sa:
तव प्रसाद प्रभु कृपानिधाना ।
मो कहुँ सर्ब काल कल्याना ॥
verses.tr:
tav prasād prabhu kṛpānidhānā
mo kahum̐ sarb kāl kalyānā

verses.sa:
एवमस्तु कहि कपटमुनि बोला कुटिल बहोरि ।
मिलब हमार भुलाब निज कहहु त हमहि न खोरि ॥
verses.tr:
evamastu kahi kapaṭamuni bolā kuṭil bahori
milab hamār bhulāb nij kahahu ta hamahi na khori
verses.head: दोहा

trans: Said the anchorite,—“ O king, so be it; there is, however, one difficulty; hear it. Theage shall bow down before you, with the sole exception of the Brahmans. By the virtue of penance a Brahman is ever powerful, and there is none who can deliver from his wrath. If you can reduce them to your will, Brahma, Vishnu and Mahadeva will also be at your command. But against a Brahman might is of no avail: with both arms raised to heaven I tell you this solemn truth. Hearken, O King, if you escape a Brahman's curse, your destruction shall never be.” On hearing his promise the king was glad,—“ Then, my lord, my destruction will never be; by your favour, most gracious sir, I shall be prosperous for all time.”

sections.label: Doha 166
sections.name: होहिं बिप्र बस कवन बिधि कहहु कृपा करि सोउ

verses.sa:
तातें मै तोहि बरजउँ राजा ।
कहें कथा तव परम अकाजा ॥
verses.tr:
tāteṃ mai tohi barajaum̐ rājā
kaheṃ kathā tav param akājā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
छठें श्रवन यह परत कहानी ।
नास तुम्हार सत्य मम बानी ॥
verses.tr:
chaṭheṃ śravan yah parat kahānī
nās tumhār satya mam bānī

verses.sa:
यह प्रगटें अथवा द्विजश्रापा ।
नास तोर सुनु भानुप्रतापा ॥
verses.tr:
yah pragaṭeṃ athavā dvijaśrāpā
nās tor sunu bhānupratāpā

verses.sa:
आन उपायँ निधन तव नाहीं ।
जौं हरि हर कोपहिं मन माहीं ॥
verses.tr:
ān upāyam̐ nidhan tav nāhīṃ
jauṃ hari har kopahiṃ man māhīṃ

verses.sa:
सत्य नाथ पद गहि नृप भाषा ।
द्विज गुर कोप कहहु को राखा ॥
verses.tr:
satya nāth pad gahi nṛp bhāṣā
dvij gur kop kahahu ko rākhā

verses.sa:
राखइ गुर जौं कोप बिधाता ।
गुर बिरोध नहिं कोउ जग त्राता ॥
verses.tr:
rākhai gur jauṃ kop bidhātā
gur birodh nahiṃ kou jag trātā

verses.sa:
जौं न चलब हम कहे तुम्हारें ।
होउ नास नहिं सोच हमारें ॥
verses.tr:
jauṃ na calab ham kahe tumhāreṃ
hou nās nahiṃ soc hamāreṃ

verses.sa:
एकहिं डर डरपत मन मोरा ।
प्रभु महिदेव श्राप अति घोरा ॥
verses.tr:
ekahiṃ ḍar ḍarapat man morā
prabhu mahidev śrāp ati ghorā

verses.sa:
होहिं बिप्र बस कवन बिधि कहहु कृपा करि सोउ ।
तुम्ह तजि दीनदयाल निज हितू न देखउँ कोउँ ॥
verses.tr:
hohiṃ bipr bas kavan bidhi kahahu kṛpā kari sou
tumh taji dīnadayāl nij hitū na dekhaum̐ koum̐
verses.head: दोहा

trans: “For I warn you, sir, that it is most inexpedient to repeat the matter: if it come to a third pair of ears, I tell you true it will be your ruin. If you divulge this secret, or if a Brahman curse you, you are undone, O Pratapabhanu. When Hari and Hara are wroth, wretched man has no other way of escape.” ‘True, my lord,” said the king, clasping his feet; ‘who can deliver from the wrath of a Brahman or a spiritual director? The guru can save from Brahma's anger, but if the gara himself be wroth, there is none in the world that can save. IfI do not follow your advice, I have not the slightest doubt that I shall perish; but my soul is disturbed by one fear; the curse of a Brahman is something
“OF your great goodness, tell mein what way I can win over the Brahmans; for except you, my gracious lord I have no other friend.”

sections.label: Doha 167
sections.name: अस कहि गहे नरेस पद स्वामी होहु कृपाल

verses.sa:
सुनु नृप बिबिध जतन जग माहीं ।
कष्टसाध्य पुनि होहिं कि नाहीं ॥
verses.tr:
sunu nṛp bibidh jatan jag māhīṃ
kaṣṭasādhya puni hohiṃ ki nāhīṃ
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
अहइ एक अति सुगम उपाई ।
तहाँ परंतु एक कठिनाई ॥
verses.tr:
ahai ek ati sugam upāī
tahām̐ paraṃtu ek kaṭhināī

verses.sa:
मम आधीन जुगुति नृप सोई ।
मोर जाब तव नगर न होई ॥
verses.tr:
mam ādhīn juguti nṛp soī
mor jāb tav nagar na hoī

verses.sa:
आजु लगें अरु जब तें भयऊँ ।
काहू के गृह ग्राम न गयऊँ ॥
verses.tr:
āju lageṃ aru jab teṃ bhayaūm̐
kāhū ke gṛh grām na gayaūm̐

verses.sa:
जौं न जाउँ तव होइ अकाजू ।
बना आइ असमंजस आजू ॥
verses.tr:
jauṃ na jāum̐ tav hoi akājū
banā āi asamaṃjas ājū

verses.sa:
सुनि महीस बोलेउ मृदु बानी ।
नाथ निगम असि नीति बखानी ॥
verses.tr:
suni mahīs boleu mṛdu bānī
nāth nigam asi nīti bakhānī

verses.sa:
बड़े सनेह लघुन्ह पर करहीं ।
गिरि निज सिरनि सदा तृन धरहीं ॥
verses.tr:
bar̤e saneh laghunh par karahīṃ
giri nij sirani sadā tṛn dharahīṃ

verses.sa:
जलधि अगाध मौलि बह फेनू ।
संतत धरनि धरत सिर रेनू ॥
verses.tr:
jaladhi agādh mauli bah phenū
saṃtat dharani dharat sir renū

verses.sa:
अस कहि गहे नरेस पद स्वामी होहु कृपाल ।
मोहि लागि दुख सहिअ प्रभु सज्जन दीनदयाल ॥
verses.tr:
as kahi gahe nares pad svāmī hohu kṛpāl
mohi lāgi dukh sahia prabhu sajjan dīnadayāl
verses.head: दोहा

trans: “Hearken, O king, there are diverse expedients among men, but hard to put in practice and of doubtful issue. There is, however, one very simple plan, though even this involves a difficulty. Its contrivance depends upon me, and for me to go to your capital is out of the question; for to this day from the time I was born I have never entered house or village. I€ I do not go, it will be a misfortune for you;and thusJ amin a dilemma.” The king replied in gentle tones, —“ It is, my lord, a maxim of scripture that the great show kindness to the small; thus mountains ever bear tiny grasses on their head; the fathomless ocean bears on itsfront the floating foam, and earth on its head bears the dust.”
Thus saying and embracing his feet, the king cried, — * Be gracious, O my lord, ever pitiful to the faithful in distress, and take this trouble on my behalf.”’

sections.label: Doha 168
sections.name: नित नूतन द्विज सहस सत बरेहु सहित परिवार

verses.sa:
जानि नृपहि आपन आधीना ।
बोला तापस कपट प्रबीना ॥
verses.tr:
jāni nṛpahi āpan ādhīnā
bolā tāpas kapaṭ prabīnā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
सत्य कहउँ भूपति सुनु तोही ।
जग नाहिन दुर्लभ कछु मोही ॥
verses.tr:
satya kahaum̐ bhūpati sunu tohī
jag nāhin durlabh kachu mohī

verses.sa:
अवसि काज मैं करिहउँ तोरा ।
मन तन बचन भगत तैं मोरा ॥
verses.tr:
avasi kāj maiṃ karihaum̐ torā
man tan bacan bhagat taiṃ morā

verses.sa:
जोग जुगुति तप मंत्र प्रभाऊ ।
फलइ तबहिं जब करिअ दुराऊ ॥
verses.tr:
jog juguti tap maṃtr prabhāū
phalai tabahiṃ jab karia durāū

verses.sa:
जौं नरेस मैं करौं रसोई ।
तुम्ह परुसहु मोहि जान न कोई ॥
verses.tr:
jauṃ nares maiṃ karauṃ rasoī
tumh parusahu mohi jān na koī

verses.sa:
अन्न सो जोइ जोइ भोजन करई ।
सोइ सोइ तव आयसु अनुसरई ॥
verses.tr:
ann so joi joi bhojan karaī
soi soi tav āyasu anusaraī

verses.sa:
पुनि तिन्ह के गृह जेवँइ जोऊ ।
तव बस होइ भूप सुनु सोऊ ॥
verses.tr:
puni tinh ke gṛh jevam̐i joū
tav bas hoi bhūp sunu soū

verses.sa:
जाइ उपाय रचहु नृप एहू ।
संबत भरि संकलप करेहू ॥
verses.tr:
jāi upāya racahu nṛp ehū
saṃbat bhari saṃkalap karehū

verses.sa:
नित नूतन द्विज सहस सत बरेहु सहित परिवार ।
मैं तुम्हरे संकलप लगि दिनहिंकरिब जेवनार ॥
verses.tr:
nit nūtan dvij sahas sat barehu sahit parivār
maiṃ tumhare saṃkalap lagi dinahiṃkarib jevanār
verses.head: दोहा

trans: Perceiving that the king was altogether under his influence, the hermit, the arch-deceiver, said,—‘ Hearken, O king; I tell you truly there is nothing in the world I cannot do, and as you show yourself in thought, word and action to be devoted to me, I will assuredly accomplish your object for you. The power of magical devices, penance and spells works only when secrecy is maintained. If, O king, I act as cook and serve, without any one knowing me, whoever tastes the food so prepared shall become amenable to your orders; and, further, any one who eats in their house will, I tell you, bein your power. Go now and carry out this scheme: make a vow for a whole year,
and every day entertain a new set of a hundred thousand Brahmans with their families; while I, as long as the vow lasts, will provide the daily banquet.

sections.label: Doha 169
sections.name: मैं आउब सोइ बेषु धरि पहिचानेहु तब मोहि

verses.sa:
एहि बिधि भूप कष्ट अति थोरें ।
होइहहिं सकल बिप्र बस तोरें ॥
verses.tr:
ehi bidhi bhūp kaṣṭ ati thoreṃ
hoihahiṃ sakal bipr bas toreṃ
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
करिहहिं बिप्र होम मख सेवा ।
तेहिं प्रसंग सहजेहिं बस देवा ॥
verses.tr:
karihahiṃ bipr hom makh sevā
tehiṃ prasaṃg sahajehiṃ bas devā

verses.sa:
और एक तोहि कहऊँ लखाऊ ।
मैं एहि बेष न आउब काऊ ॥
verses.tr:
aur ek tohi kahaūm̐ lakhāū
maiṃ ehi beṣ na āub kāū

verses.sa:
तुम्हरे उपरोहित कहुँ राया ।
हरि आनब मैं करि निज माया ॥
verses.tr:
tumhare uparohit kahum̐ rāyā
hari ānab maiṃ kari nij māyā

verses.sa:
तपबल तेहि करि आपु समाना ।
रखिहउँ इहाँ बरष परवाना ॥
verses.tr:
tapabal tehi kari āpu samānā
rakhihaum̐ ihām̐ baraṣ paravānā

verses.sa:
मैं धरि तासु बेषु सुनु राजा ।
सब बिधि तोर सँवारब काजा ॥
verses.tr:
maiṃ dhari tāsu beṣu sunu rājā
sab bidhi tor sam̐vārab kājā

verses.sa:
गै निसि बहुत सयन अब कीजे ।
मोहि तोहि भूप भेंट दिन तीजे ॥
verses.tr:
gai nisi bahut sayan ab kīje
mohi tohi bhūp bheṃṭ din tīje

verses.sa:
मैं तपबल तोहि तुरग समेता ।
पहुँचेहउँ सोवतहि निकेता ॥
verses.tr:
maiṃ tapabal tohi turag sametā
pahum̐cehaum̐ sovatahi niketā

verses.sa:
मैं आउब सोइ बेषु धरि पहिचानेहु तब मोहि ।
जब एकांत बोलाइ सब कथा सुनावौं तोहि ॥
verses.tr:
maiṃ āub soi beṣu dhari pahicānehu tab mohi
jab ekāṃt bolāi sab kathā sunāvauṃ tohi
verses.head: दोहा

trans: “In this way, O king, there will be very little trouble, and all the Brahmans will be in your power. They again will perform sacrificial services, and thus the gods, too, will be easily won over. And I will give you a sign. I will not come in this dress, but by my delusive power I will bring away your family priest, and by the virtue of penance will make him look like myself and keep him here for the year; while I in his form will manage everything for you. The night is far gone, so now take rest; on the third day we will meet again. While you are asleep 1, by my penitential power, will convey you home, both you and your horse.
‘I will then come in the form I have told you, and you will recognize me when I call you on one side and remind you of all this.”

sections.label: Doha 170
sections.name: रिपु तेजसी अकेल अपि लघु करि गनिअ न ताहु

verses.sa:
सयन कीन्ह नृप आयसु मानी ।
आसन जाइ बैठ छलग्यानी ॥
verses.tr:
sayan kīnh nṛp āyasu mānī
āsan jāi baiṭh chalagyānī
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
श्रमित भूप निद्रा अति आई ।
सो किमि सोव सोच अधिकाई ॥
verses.tr:
śramit bhūp nidrā ati āī
so kimi sov soc adhikāī

verses.sa:
कालकेतु निसिचर तहँ आवा ।
जेहिं सूकर होइ नृपहि भुलावा ॥
verses.tr:
kālaketu nisicar taham̐ āvā
jehiṃ sūkar hoi nṛpahi bhulāvā

verses.sa:
परम मित्र तापस नृप केरा ।
जानइ सो अति कपट घनेरा ॥
verses.tr:
param mitr tāpas nṛp kerā
jānai so ati kapaṭ ghanerā

verses.sa:
तेहि के सत सुत अरु दस भाई ।
खल अति अजय देव दुखदाई ॥
verses.tr:
tehi ke sat sut aru das bhāī
khal ati ajaya dev dukhadāī

verses.sa:
प्रथमहि भूप समर सब मारे ।
बिप्र संत सुर देखि दुखारे ॥
verses.tr:
prathamahi bhūp samar sab māre
bipr saṃt sur dekhi dukhāre

verses.sa:
तेहिं खल पाछिल बयरु सँभरा ।
तापस नृप मिलि मंत्र बिचारा ॥
verses.tr:
tehiṃ khal pāchil bayaru sam̐bharā
tāpas nṛp mili maṃtr bicārā

verses.sa:
जेहि रिपु छय सोइ रचेन्हि उपाऊ ।
भावी बस न जान कछु राऊ ॥
verses.tr:
jehi ripu chaya soi racenhi upāū
bhāvī bas na jān kachu rāū

verses.sa:
रिपु तेजसी अकेल अपि लघु करि गनिअ न ताहु ।
अजहुँ देत दुख रबि ससिहि सिर अवसेषित राहु ॥
verses.tr:
ripu tejasī akel api laghu kari gania na tāhu
ajahum̐ det dukh rabi sasihi sir avaseṣit rāhu
verses.head: दोहा

trans: The king, as ordered, retired to his couch, while the archdeceiver took his wonted seat. Deep sleep came upon the weary king; but what sleep for the other, distraught with care? Then came the demon Kaluketu, who was the boar that had led the king astray, a great friend of the hermit king, and skilled in manifold ways of deceit. He had a hundred sons and ten brothers, unmatched in villainy, the torment of the gods; but they had all before this been killed in battle by the king, who saw the distress they had caused to the Br^hmans, saints and powers of heaven. The wretch, nursing this old quarrel, combined with the hermit king in devising a plot for the destruction of his enemy. The prince, overmastered by fate, knew nothing of it.
A powerful foe, even though surprised alone, is not to be lightly regarded; to this day Raehu, though he has nothing left but his head, is able to annoy both sun and moon.

sections.label: Doha 171
sections.name: राजा के उपरोहितहि हरि लै गयउ बहोरि

verses.sa:
तापस नृप निज सखहि निहारी ।
हरषि मिलेउ उठि भयउ सुखारी ॥
verses.tr:
tāpas nṛp nij sakhahi nihārī
haraṣi mileu uṭhi bhayau sukhārī
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
मित्रहि कहि सब कथा सुनाई ।
जातुधान बोला सुख पाई ॥
verses.tr:
mitrahi kahi sab kathā sunāī
jātudhān bolā sukh pāī

verses.sa:
अब साधेउँ रिपु सुनहु नरेसा ।
जौं तुम्ह कीन्ह मोर उपदेसा ॥
verses.tr:
ab sādheum̐ ripu sunahu naresā
jauṃ tumh kīnh mor upadesā

verses.sa:
परिहरि सोच रहहु तुम्ह सोई ।
बिनु औषध बिआधि बिधि खोई ॥
verses.tr:
parihari soc rahahu tumh soī
binu auṣadh biādhi bidhi khoī

verses.sa:
कुल समेत रिपु मूल बहाई ।
चौथे दिवस मिलब मैं आई ॥
verses.tr:
kul samet ripu mūl bahāī
cauthe divas milab maiṃ āī

verses.sa:
तापस नृपहि बहुत परितोषी ।
चला महाकपटी अतिरोषी ॥
verses.tr:
tāpas nṛpahi bahut paritoṣī
calā mahākapaṭī atiroṣī

verses.sa:
भानुप्रतापहि बाजि समेता ।
पहुँचाएसि छन माझ निकेता ॥
verses.tr:
bhānupratāpahi bāji sametā
pahum̐cāesi chan mājh niketā

verses.sa:
नृपहि नारि पहिं सयन कराई ।
हयगृहँ बाँधेसि बाजि बनाई ॥
verses.tr:
nṛpahi nāri pahiṃ sayan karāī
hayagṛham̐ bām̐dhesi bāji banāī

verses.sa:
राजा के उपरोहितहि हरि लै गयउ बहोरि ।
लै राखेसि गिरि खोह महुँ मायाँ करि मति भोरि ॥
verses.tr:
rājā ke uparohitahi hari lai gayau bahori
lai rākhesi giri khoh mahum̐ māyām̐ kari mati bhori
verses.head: दोहा

trans: When the hermit king saw his ally, he rose in great joy to meet him, and told his friend the whole story. The demon was glad and said,—“ Hear, O king, Tam ready to settle your enemy if you will take my advice. — Free yourself of all anxiety and sleep quietly here: without

taking any medicine God has cured your complaint, I will sweep away the enemy, root and branch, and in four days will be back again.” Having thus cheered the hermit king, the arch-deceiver went away in his wrath, and conveyed to the palace Pratdepabhenn still asleep, both him and his horse; the king he put to bed beside his queen, and the horse he tied up in the stall, Doha 175.
Again he carried off the king’s family priest, and by supernatural power depriving him of his senses, kept him in a cave in the mountain,

sections.label: Doha 172
sections.name: नृप हरषेउ पहिचानि गुरु भ्रम बस रहा न चेत

verses.sa:
आपु बिरचि उपरोहित रूपा ।
परेउ जाइ तेहि सेज अनूपा ॥
verses.tr:
āpu biraci uparohit rūpā
pareu jāi tehi sej anūpā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
जागेउ नृप अनभएँ बिहाना ।
देखि भवन अति अचरजु माना ॥
verses.tr:
jāgeu nṛp anabhaem̐ bihānā
dekhi bhavan ati acaraju mānā

verses.sa:
मुनि महिमा मन महुँ अनुमानी ।
उठेउ गवँहि जेहि जान न रानी ॥
verses.tr:
muni mahimā man mahum̐ anumānī
uṭheu gavam̐hi jehi jān na rānī

verses.sa:
कानन गयउ बाजि चढ़ि तेहीं ।
पुर नर नारि न जानेउ केहीं ॥
verses.tr:
kānan gayau bāji car̤hi tehīṃ
pur nar nāri na jāneu kehīṃ

verses.sa:
गएँ जाम जुग भूपति आवा ।
घर घर उत्सव बाज बधावा ॥
verses.tr:
gaem̐ jām jug bhūpati āvā
ghar ghar utsav bāj badhāvā

verses.sa:
उपरोहितहि देख जब राजा ।
चकित बिलोकि सुमिरि सोइ काजा ॥
verses.tr:
uparohitahi dekh jab rājā
cakit biloki sumiri soi kājā

verses.sa:
जुग सम नृपहि गए दिन तीनी ।
कपटी मुनि पद रह मति लीनी ॥
verses.tr:
jug sam nṛpahi gae din tīnī
kapaṭī muni pad rah mati līnī

verses.sa:
समय जानि उपरोहित आवा ।
नृपहि मते सब कहि समुझावा ॥
verses.tr:
samaya jāni uparohit āvā
nṛpahi mate sab kahi samujhāvā

verses.sa:
नृप हरषेउ पहिचानि गुरु भ्रम बस रहा न चेत ।
बरे तुरत सत सहस बर बिप्र कुटुंब समेत ॥
verses.tr:
nṛp haraṣeu pahicāni guru bhram bas rahā na cet
bare turat sat sahas bar bipr kuṭuṃb samet
verses.head: दोहा

trans: While he himself assumed the priests form and went and lay down on his sumptuouscouch. At daybreak the king woke and was astonished to find himself at home. Much impressed with the hermit’s power, he rose and went out unperceived by the queen, and mounting his horse rode off the wood without any of the people in the city knowing it. When it was noon he returned, and in every house there was rejoicing, with music and singing. When he saw the family priest, he looked at him in amazement, remembering the work in hand, The three days seemed like an age, so absorbed was he in expectation of the false hermit’s coming. When the appointed time had come, the priest took the king and told him the whole plot.
The king was delighted to recognize the guru, and was too infatuated to have any sense left, but at once sent and invited a hundred thousand Brahmans with their families.

sections.label: Doha 173
sections.name: बोले बिप्र सकोप तब नहिं कछु कीन्ह बिचार

verses.sa:
उपरोहित जेवनार बनाई ।
छरस चारि बिधि जसि श्रुति गाई ॥
verses.tr:
uparohit jevanār banāī
charas cāri bidhi jasi śruti gāī
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
मायामय तेहिं कीन्ह रसोई ।
बिंजन बहु गनि सकइ न कोई ॥
verses.tr:
māyāmaya tehiṃ kīnh rasoī
biṃjan bahu gani sakai na koī

verses.sa:
बिबिध मृगन्ह कर आमिष राँधा ।
तेहि महुँ बिप्र माँसु खल साँधा ॥
verses.tr:
bibidh mṛganh kar āmiṣ rām̐dhā
tehi mahum̐ bipr mām̐su khal sām̐dhā

verses.sa:
भोजन कहुँ सब बिप्र बोलाए ।
पद पखारि सादर बैठाए ॥
verses.tr:
bhojan kahum̐ sab bipr bolāe
pad pakhāri sādar baiṭhāe

verses.sa:
परुसन जबहिं लाग महिपाला ।
भै अकासबानी तेहि काला ॥
verses.tr:
parusan jabahiṃ lāg mahipālā
bhai akāsabānī tehi kālā

verses.sa:
बिप्रबृंद उठि उठि गृह जाहू ।
है बड़ि हानि अन्न जनि खाहू ॥
verses.tr:
biprabṛṃd uṭhi uṭhi gṛh jāhū
hai bar̤i hāni ann jani khāhū

verses.sa:
भयउ रसोईं भूसुर माँसू ।
सब द्विज उठे मानि बिस्वासू ॥
verses.tr:
bhayau rasoīṃ bhūsur mām̐sū
sab dvij uṭhe māni bisvāsū

verses.sa:
भूप बिकल मति मोहँ भुलानी ।
भावी बस आव मुख बानी ॥
verses.tr:
bhūp bikal mati moham̐ bhulānī
bhāvī bas āv mukh bānī

verses.sa:
बोले बिप्र सकोप तब नहिं कछु कीन्ह बिचार ।
जाइ निसाचर होहु नृप मूढ़ सहित परिवार ॥
verses.tr:
bole bipr sakop tab nahiṃ kachu kīnh bicār
jāi nisācar hohu nṛp mūr̤h sahit parivār
verses.head: दोहा

trans: The priest superintended the cooking, and in accordance with sacred prescription concocted the six tastes in the four different ways', preparing a most seductive banquet, with sauces and condiments more than any one could count. After dressing agreat variety of meat, the wretch introduced into the dish some pieces of a Brahman’s flesh. He then summoned all the Brahmans to the feast and washed their feet and politely showed them to their places. But directly they began to touch the food, « voice came from heaven, — ‘Up, up, all ye Brahmans and return to your homes; though the loss be great, yet taste not the food; there is Brahman's flesh in the dish.” Up rose all the holy men, believing the heavenly voice; while the king, distracted and out of his senses, over-mastered by fate, could not utter a word. Dohe 177.
Then cried the Brahmans in their wrath, regardless of what must follow, —‘ O foolish king, take birth in demon’s form yourself and all your family.

sections.label: Doha 174
sections.name: भूपति भावी मिटइ नहिं जदपि न दूषन तोर

verses.sa:
छत्रबंधु तैं बिप्र बोलाई ।
घालै लिए सहित समुदाई ॥
verses.tr:
chatrabaṃdhu taiṃ bipr bolāī
ghālai lie sahit samudāī
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
ईस्वर राखा धरम हमारा ।
जैहसि तैं समेत परिवारा ॥
verses.tr:
īsvar rākhā dharam hamārā
jaihasi taiṃ samet parivārā

verses.sa:
संबत मध्य नास तव होऊ ।
जलदाता न रहिहि कुल कोऊ ॥
verses.tr:
saṃbat madhya nās tav hoū
jaladātā na rahihi kul koū

verses.sa:
नृप सुनि श्राप बिकल अति त्रासा ।
भै बहोरि बर गिरा अकासा ॥
verses.tr:
nṛp suni śrāp bikal ati trāsā
bhai bahori bar girā akāsā

verses.sa:
बिप्रहु श्राप बिचारि न दीन्हा ।
नहिं अपराध भूप कछु कीन्हा ॥
verses.tr:
biprahu śrāp bicāri na dīnhā
nahiṃ aparādh bhūp kachu kīnhā

verses.sa:
चकित बिप्र सब सुनि नभबानी ।
भूप गयउ जहँ भोजन खानी ॥
verses.tr:
cakit bipr sab suni nabhabānī
bhūp gayau jaham̐ bhojan khānī

verses.sa:
तहँ न असन नहिं बिप्र सुआरा ।
फिरेउ राउ मन सोच अपारा ॥
verses.tr:
taham̐ na asan nahiṃ bipr suārā
phireu rāu man soc apārā

verses.sa:
सब प्रसंग महिसुरन्ह सुनाई ।
त्रसित परेउ अवनीं अकुलाई ॥
verses.tr:
sab prasaṃg mahisuranh sunāī
trasit pareu avanīṃ akulāī

verses.sa:
भूपति भावी मिटइ नहिं जदपि न दूषन तोर ।
किएँ अन्यथा होइ नहिं बिप्रश्राप अति घोर ॥
verses.tr:
bhūpati bhāvī miṭai nahiṃ jadapi na dūṣan tor
kiem̐ anyathā hoi nahiṃ bipraśrāp ati ghor
verses.head: दोहा

trans: “O noble prince, you invited all this Brehmanical come pany here simply to destroy us; God has preserved our honour, and it is you and your race who are undone. You shall perish in the midst of your days, nor shall there be one left to offer libations to your ghost.” When the king heard the curse he was terror-stricken. Again a voice came from heaven, —‘“ The Brahmans have uttered this curse without due consideration, the king has committed no crime.” All the Br^hmans were astounded when they heard the heavenly voice. The king hastened to the kitchen; there he found neither food nor Brahmans cook, and he turned away in deep thought, declared the whole history to the Brahmans, and io his terror and distress threw himself upon the ground.
“Though you, O king are guiltless, what is fated fails not; the past is unalterable; a Brahman's curse is a terrible thing.”

sections.label: Doha 175
sections.name: भरद्वाज सुनु जाहि जब होइ बिधाता बाम

verses.sa:
अस कहि सब महिदेव सिधाए ।
समाचार पुरलोगन्ह पाए ॥
verses.tr:
as kahi sab mahidev sidhāe
samācār puraloganh pāe
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
सोचहिं दूषन दैवहि देहीं ।
बिचरत हंस काग किय जेहीं ॥
verses.tr:
socahiṃ dūṣan daivahi dehīṃ
bicarat haṃs kāg kiya jehīṃ

verses.sa:
उपरोहितहि भवन पहुँचाई ।
असुर तापसहि खबरि जनाई ॥
verses.tr:
uparohitahi bhavan pahum̐cāī
asur tāpasahi khabari janāī

verses.sa:
तेहिं खल जहँ तहँ पत्र पठाए ।
सजि सजि सेन भूप सब धाए ॥
verses.tr:
tehiṃ khal jaham̐ taham̐ patr paṭhāe
saji saji sen bhūp sab dhāe

verses.sa:
घेरेन्हि नगर निसान बजाई ।
बिबिध भाँति नित होई लराई ॥
verses.tr:
gherenhi nagar nisān bajāī
bibidh bhām̐ti nit hoī larāī

verses.sa:
जूझे सकल सुभट करि करनी ।
बंधु समेत परेउ नृप धरनी ॥
verses.tr:
jūjhe sakal subhaṭ kari karanī
baṃdhu samet pareu nṛp dharanī

verses.sa:
सत्यकेतु कुल कोउ नहिं बाँचा ।
बिप्रश्राप किमि होइ असाँचा ॥
verses.tr:
satyaketu kul kou nahiṃ bām̐cā
bipraśrāp kimi hoi asām̐cā

verses.sa:
रिपु जिति सब नृप नगर बसाई ।
निज पुर गवने जय जसु पाई ॥
verses.tr:
ripu jiti sab nṛp nagar basāī
nij pur gavane jaya jasu pāī

verses.sa:
भरद्वाज सुनु जाहि जब होइ बिधाता बाम ।
धूरि मेरुसम जनक जम ताहि ब्यालसम दाम ॥
verses.tr:
bharadvāj sunu jāhi jab hoi bidhātā bām
dhūri merusam janak jam tāhi byālasam dām
verses.head: दोहा

trans: So saying, all the Br^hmans went their way. When the people of the city heard the news, they were much vexed and abused Fate, who had begun upon a swan and ended in making crow. ‘The demon conveyed the family priest to the palace and told the hermit all the tidings. Then the wretch despatched letters in all directions; a host of princes came in with their troops, and with blast of trumpets beleagured the city. Day after day there were battles of various kinds; all his champions fell in fight, after doing valorously, and the king with his brother bit

the dust. Not one of Satyaketu’s family escaped, for a Brahman's curse can never fail of accomplishment. Triumphing over their foe, the chiefs refounded the city, and then, crowned with victory, returned to their own states.
Hearken, Bharadv4ja, whoever incurs the ‘anger of heaven, for him a grain of dust becomes vast as Mount Meru, a father like the angel of death, and every rope a snake.

sections.label: Doha 176
sections.name: उपजे जदपि पुलस्त्यकुल पावन अमल अनूप

verses.sa:
काल पाइ मुनि सुनु सोइ राजा ।
भयउ निसाचर सहित समाजा ॥
verses.tr:
kāl pāi muni sunu soi rājā
bhayau nisācar sahit samājā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
दस सिर ताहि बीस भुजदंडा ।
रावन नाम बीर बरिबंडा ॥
verses.tr:
das sir tāhi bīs bhujadaṃḍā
rāvan nām bīr baribaṃḍā

verses.sa:
भूप अनुज अरिमर्दन नामा ।
भयउ सो कुंभकरन बलधामा ॥
verses.tr:
bhūp anuj arimardan nāmā
bhayau so kuṃbhakaran baladhāmā

verses.sa:
सचिव जो रहा धरमरुचि जासू ।
भयउ बिमात्र बंधु लघु तासू ॥
verses.tr:
saciv jo rahā dharamaruci jāsū
bhayau bimātr baṃdhu laghu tāsū

verses.sa:
नाम बिभीषन जेहि जग जाना ।
बिष्नुभगत बिग्यान निधाना ॥
verses.tr:
nām bibhīṣan jehi jag jānā
biṣnubhagat bigyān nidhānā

verses.sa:
रहे जे सुत सेवक नृप केरे ।
भए निसाचर घोर घनेरे ॥
verses.tr:
rahe je sut sevak nṛp kere
bhae nisācar ghor ghanere

verses.sa:
कामरूप खल जिनस अनेका ।
कुटिल भयंकर बिगत बिबेका ॥
verses.tr:
kāmarūp khal jinas anekā
kuṭil bhayaṃkar bigat bibekā

verses.sa:
कृपा रहित हिंसक सब पापी ।
बरनि न जाहिं बिस्व परितापी ॥
verses.tr:
kṛpā rahit hiṃsak sab pāpī
barani na jāhiṃ bisv paritāpī

verses.sa:
उपजे जदपि पुलस्त्यकुल पावन अमल अनूप ।
तदपि महीसुर श्राप बस भए सकल अघरूप ॥
verses.tr:
upaje jadapi pulastyakul pāvan amal anūp
tadapi mahīsur śrāp bas bhae sakal agharūp
verses.head: दोहा

trans: Hearken, reverend sir; in due time this Raja, with his family, was born as a demon with ten heads and twenty arms, a formidable hero, by name Ravan. The king’s younger brother, Ari-mardan, became the valiant Kumbha- Karn, while the minister Dharma-ruchi became his half-brother, the world-famous Vibhishan, the all-wise votary of Vishnu. As for the king’s sons and servants, they were born a fierce demon crew; wretches, taking various shapes at will: wicked, monstrous and devoid of knowledge; merciless, injarious, criminal—a torment to all creation beyond what words can tell.
Though born in the incomparably pure and holy family of Pulastya, yet on account of the Br^hmans’ curse all were of hateful mien.

sections.label: Doha 177
sections.name: गए बिभीषन पास पुनि कहेउ पुत्र बर मागु

verses.sa:
कीन्ह बिबिध तप तीनिहुँ भाई ।
परम उग्र नहिं बरनि सो जाई ॥
verses.tr:
kīnh bibidh tap tīnihum̐ bhāī
param ugr nahiṃ barani so jāī
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
गयउ निकट तप देखि बिधाता ।
मागहु बर प्रसन्न मैं ताता ॥
verses.tr:
gayau nikaṭ tap dekhi bidhātā
māgahu bar prasann maiṃ tātā

verses.sa:
करि बिनती पद गहि दससीसा ।
बोलेउ बचन सुनहु जगदीसा ॥
verses.tr:
kari binatī pad gahi dasasīsā
boleu bacan sunahu jagadīsā

verses.sa:
हम काहू के मरहिं न मारें ।
बानर मनुज जाति दुइ बारें ॥
verses.tr:
ham kāhū ke marahiṃ na māreṃ
bānar manuj jāti dui bāreṃ

verses.sa:
एवमस्तु तुम्ह बड़ तप कीन्हा ।
मैं ब्रह्माँ मिलि तेहि बर दीन्हा ॥
verses.tr:
evamastu tumh bar̤ tap kīnhā
maiṃ brahmām̐ mili tehi bar dīnhā

verses.sa:
पुनि प्रभु कुंभकरन पहिं गयऊ ।
तेहि बिलोकि मन बिसमय भयऊ ॥
verses.tr:
puni prabhu kuṃbhakaran pahiṃ gayaū
tehi biloki man bisamaya bhayaū

verses.sa:
जौं एहिं खल नित करब अहारू ।
होइहि सब उजारि संसारू ॥
verses.tr:
jauṃ ehiṃ khal nit karab ahārū
hoihi sab ujāri saṃsārū

verses.sa:
सारद प्रेरि तासु मति फेरी ।
मागेसि नीद मास षट केरी ॥
verses.tr:
sārad preri tāsu mati pherī
māgesi nīd mās ṣaṭ kerī

verses.sa:
गए बिभीषन पास पुनि कहेउ पुत्र बर मागु ।
तेहिं मागेउ भगवंत पद कमल अमल अनुरागु ॥
verses.tr:
gae bibhīṣan pās puni kaheu putr bar māgu
tehiṃ māgeu bhagavaṃt pad kamal amal anurāgu
verses.head: दोहा

trans: The three brothers practised manifold penitential observances, severe beyond all description; the Creator drew nigh to witness them, and said,—“ Son, I am well pleased, ask a boon.” The Ten-headed suppliantly clasped his feet and cried,—“ Hear, O lord of earth: I would die at the hand of none save man or monkey.” Brahma and I granted him his boon, saying,—‘So be it; you have done great penance.” Then the lord went to Kumbha-karn, and was astounded at his appearance,—‘ If this wretch is always eating, the whole world will be laid waste.” So he sent
Sarasvati to turn his head, and he asked for six months’ slumber.
Then he went to Vibbishan and said,— Son, ask a boon:” and he asked for perfect love of God.

sections.label: Doha 178
sections.name: खाईं सिंधु गभीर अति चारिहुँ दिसि फिरि आव

verses.sa:
तिन्हि देइ बर ब्रह्म सिधाए ।
हरषित ते अपने गृह आए ॥
verses.tr:
tinhi dei bar brahm sidhāe
haraṣit te apane gṛh āe
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
मय तनुजा मंदोदरि नामा ।
परम सुंदरी नारि ललामा ॥
verses.tr:
maya tanujā maṃdodari nāmā
param suṃdarī nāri lalāmā

verses.sa:
सोइ मयँ दीन्हि रावनहि आनी ।
होइहि जातुधानपति जानी ॥
verses.tr:
soi mayam̐ dīnhi rāvanahi ānī
hoihi jātudhānapati jānī

verses.sa:
हरषित भयउ नारि भलि पाई ।
पुनि दोउ बंधु बिआहेसि जाई ॥
verses.tr:
haraṣit bhayau nāri bhali pāī
puni dou baṃdhu biāhesi jāī

verses.sa:
गिरि त्रिकूट एक सिंधु मझारी ।
बिधि निर्मित दुर्गम अति भारी ॥
verses.tr:
giri trikūṭ ek siṃdhu majhārī
bidhi nirmit durgam ati bhārī

verses.sa:
सोइ मय दानवँ बहुरि सँवारा ।
कनक रचित मनिभवन अपारा ॥
verses.tr:
soi maya dānavam̐ bahuri sam̐vārā
kanak racit manibhavan apārā

verses.sa:
भोगावति जसि अहिकुल बासा ।
अमरावति जसि सक्रनिवासा ॥
verses.tr:
bhogāvati jasi ahikul bāsā
amarāvati jasi sakranivāsā

verses.sa:
तिन्ह तें अधिक रम्य अति बंका ।
जग बिख्यात नाम तेहि लंका ॥
verses.tr:
tinh teṃ adhik ramya ati baṃkā
jag bikhyāt nām tehi laṃkā

verses.sa:
खाईं सिंधु गभीर अति चारिहुँ दिसि फिरि आव ।
कनक कोट मनि खचित दृढ़ बरनि न जाइ बनाव ॥
verses.tr:
khāīṃ siṃdhu gabhīr ati cārihum̐ disi phiri āv
kanak koṭ mani khacit dṛr̤h barani na jāi banāv
verses.head: दोहा

verses.sa:
हरिप्रेरित जेहिं कलप जोइ जातुधानपति होइ ।
सूर प्रतापी अतुलबल दल समेत बस सोइ ॥
verses.tr:
hariprerit jehiṃ kalap joi jātudhānapati hoi
sūr pratāpī atulabal dal samet bas soi

trans: After granting these boons Brahma departed, and they went home rejoicing. Now Maya had a daughter by name Mandodari, of exceeding beauty, a jewel of womankind, whom her father brought and made over to Ravan, and she became the demon’s head-queen. Delighted at having obtained so good a wife, he next went and married his two brothers. In the middle of the ocean is a three peaked mountain, by Brahma’s contrivance most difficult of access. Here the demon Maya had constructed a vast palace of gold and jewels, more beautiful and charming than Bhogavati, the city of the serpent kings, or Indra’s capital Amaravati, and called it Lanka, a name famous throughout the world.

The deep ocean was its moat, washing its four sides; and its massive walls were of gold, set with jewelsin a way that defies description. In every age the Demon King, whom Hari predestines, lives there with his army, as a mighty and puissant chief.

sections.label: Doha 179
sections.name: कौतुकहीं कैलास पुनि लीन्हेसि जाइ उठाइ

verses.sa:
रहे तहाँ निसिचर भट भारे ।
ते सब सुरन्ह समर संघारे ॥
verses.tr:
rahe tahām̐ nisicar bhaṭ bhāre
te sab suranh samar saṃghāre
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
अब तहँ रहहिं सक्र के प्रेरे ।
रच्छक कोटि जच्छपति केरे ॥
verses.tr:
ab taham̐ rahahiṃ sakr ke prere
racchak koṭi jacchapati kere

verses.sa:
दसमुख कतहुँ खबरि असि पाई ।
सेन साजि गढ़ घेरेसि जाई ॥
verses.tr:
dasamukh katahum̐ khabari asi pāī
sen sāji gar̤h gheresi jāī

verses.sa:
देखि बिकट भट बड़ि कटकाई ।
जच्छ जीव लै गए पराई ॥
verses.tr:
dekhi bikaṭ bhaṭ bar̤i kaṭakāī
jacch jīv lai gae parāī

verses.sa:
फिरि सब नगर दसानन देखा ।
गयउ सोच सुख भयउ बिसेषा ॥
verses.tr:
phiri sab nagar dasānan dekhā
gayau soc sukh bhayau biseṣā

verses.sa:
सुंदर सहज अगम अनुमानी ।
कीन्हि तहाँ रावन रजधानी ॥
verses.tr:
suṃdar sahaj agam anumānī
kīnhi tahām̐ rāvan rajadhānī

verses.sa:
जेहि जस जोग बाँटि गृह दीन्हे ।
सुखी सकल रजनीचर कीन्हे ॥
verses.tr:
jehi jas jog bām̐ṭi gṛh dīnhe
sukhī sakal rajanīcar kīnhe

verses.sa:
एक बार कुबेर पर धावा ।
पुष्पक जान जीति लै आवा ॥
verses.tr:
ek bār kuber par dhāvā
puṣpak jān jīti lai āvā

verses.sa:
कौतुकहीं कैलास पुनि लीन्हेसि जाइ उठाइ ।
मनहुँ तौलि निज बाहुबल चला बहुत सुख पाइ ॥
verses.tr:
kautukahīṃ kailās puni līnhesi jāi uṭhāi
manahum̐ tauli nij bāhubal calā bahut sukh pāi
verses.head: दोहा

trans: There had dwelt great demon warriors, but all had been slain in battle by the gods; and now by I[ndra’s commission it was occupied by a million guards of Kuver’s. Ravan happened to hear of this, and at once marshalled his army and went and besieged the place. When the Yakshas saw the vast host of fierce warriors, they all fled for their lives. Thereupon Ravan inspected the whole of the city, and was so highly pleased with it that all his trouble was forgotten. Seeing that it was not only a beautiful, but also a naturally impregnable, site, he fixed the capital there, and assigning quarters to his followers according to their several deserts, made them all quite happy. Upon one occasion he sallied forth against Kuver, and carried away his chariot of flowers as a trophy.
Again, from mere lightness of heart, he went and overthrew Kailds, and after thus testing the prowess of his men of war, waxed yet more jubilant than before.

sections.label: Doha 180
sections.name: कुमुख अकंपन कुलिसरद धूमकेतु अतिकाय

verses.sa:
सुख संपति सुत सेन सहाई ।
जय प्रताप बल बुद्धि बड़ाई ॥
verses.tr:
sukh saṃpati sut sen sahāī
jaya pratāp bal buddhi bar̤āī
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
नित नूतन सब बाढ़त जाई ।
जिमि प्रतिलाभ लोभ अधिकाई ॥
verses.tr:
nit nūtan sab bār̤hat jāī
jimi pratilābh lobh adhikāī

verses.sa:
अतिबल कुंभकरन अस भ्राता ।
जेहि कहुँ नहिं प्रतिभट जग जाता ॥
verses.tr:
atibal kuṃbhakaran as bhrātā
jehi kahum̐ nahiṃ pratibhaṭ jag jātā

verses.sa:
करइ पान सोवइ षट मासा ।
जागत होइ तिहुँ पुर त्रासा ॥
verses.tr:
karai pān sovai ṣaṭ māsā
jāgat hoi tihum̐ pur trāsā

verses.sa:
जौं दिन प्रति अहार कर सोई ।
बिस्व बेगि सब चौपट होई ॥
verses.tr:
jauṃ din prati ahār kar soī
bisv begi sab caupaṭ hoī

verses.sa:
समर धीर नहिं जाइ बखाना ।
तेहि सम अमित बीर बलवाना ॥
verses.tr:
samar dhīr nahiṃ jāi bakhānā
tehi sam amit bīr balavānā

verses.sa:
बारिदनाद जेठ सुत तासू ।
भट महुँ प्रथम लीक जग जासू ॥
verses.tr:
bāridanād jeṭh sut tāsū
bhaṭ mahum̐ pratham līk jag jāsū

verses.sa:
जेहि न होइ रन सनमुख कोई ।
सुरपुर नितहिं परावन होई ॥
verses.tr:
jehi na hoi ran sanamukh koī
surapur nitahiṃ parāvan hoī

verses.sa:
कुमुख अकंपन कुलिसरद धूमकेतु अतिकाय ।
एक एक जग जीति सक ऐसे सुभट निकाय ॥
verses.tr:
kumukh akaṃpan kulisarad dhūmaketu atikāya
ek ek jag jīti sak aise subhaṭ nikāya
verses.head: दोहा

trans: His happiness and prosperity, the number of his sons, his army and his allies, his conquests, his might and his superior wisdom, all grew day by day more and more, in the same way as avarice grows with gain. Thus, too, his brother, the stalwart Kumbha-karn, was a champion without a match in the world. After drinking his fill he slept for six months, and at his waking the three worlds trembled. If he had taken a meal every day the whole world would soon have been stript bare: so unspeakably staunch in fight was he that no other hero could be compared to him. His eldest son was Meghn4d, who held the first place among the world’s champions; before whom none could stand in the battle; who was ever harassing the city of heaven.

And many other demons were there, each by himself able to subdue the whole world, such as the hideous Kumukh, the dauntless Akeampan, Kolisa-radd with teeth like thunderbolts the fiery Dhumra-ketu, and the huge Atikaya;

sections.label: Doha 181
sections.name: छुधा छीन बलहीन सुर सहजेहिं मिलिहहिं आइ

verses.sa:
कामरूप जानहिं सब माया ।
सपनेहुँ जिन्ह कें धरम न दाया ॥
verses.tr:
kāmarūp jānahiṃ sab māyā
sapanehum̐ jinh keṃ dharam na dāyā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
दसमुख बैठ सभाँ एक बारा ।
देखि अमित आपन परिवारा ॥
verses.tr:
dasamukh baiṭh sabhām̐ ek bārā
dekhi amit āpan parivārā

verses.sa:
सुत समूह जन परिजन नाती ।
गे को पार निसाचर जाती ॥
verses.tr:
sut samūh jan parijan nātī
ge ko pār nisācar jātī

verses.sa:
सेन बिलोकि सहज अभिमानी ।
बोला बचन क्रोध मद सानी ॥
verses.tr:
sen biloki sahaj abhimānī
bolā bacan krodh mad sānī

verses.sa:
सुनहु सकल रजनीचर जूथा ।
हमरे बैरी बिबुध बरूथा ॥
verses.tr:
sunahu sakal rajanīcar jūthā
hamare bairī bibudh barūthā

verses.sa:
ते सनमुख नहिं करही लराई ।
देखि सबल रिपु जाहिं पराई ॥
verses.tr:
te sanamukh nahiṃ karahī larāī
dekhi sabal ripu jāhiṃ parāī

verses.sa:
तेन्ह कर मरन एक बिधि होई ।
कहउँ बुझाइ सुनहु अब सोई ॥
verses.tr:
tenh kar maran ek bidhi hoī
kahaum̐ bujhāi sunahu ab soī

verses.sa:
द्विजभोजन मख होम सराधा ।
सब कै जाइ करहु तुम्ह बाधा ॥
verses.tr:
dvijabhojan makh hom sarādhā
sab kai jāi karahu tumh bādhā

verses.sa:
छुधा छीन बलहीन सुर सहजेहिं मिलिहहिं आइ ।
तब मारिहउँ कि छाड़िहउँ भली भाँति अपनाइ ॥
verses.tr:
chudhā chīn balahīn sur sahajehiṃ milihahiṃ āi
tab mārihaum̐ ki chār̤ihaum̐ bhalī bhām̐ti apanāi
verses.head: दोहा

trans: Taking form at will, skilled in every kind of fraud, without ever a thought of piety or pity. One day the Tenheaded was seated in court and reviewed his innumerable retainers, sons and grandsons, friends and servants, troops of demons, more than any one could count. On seeing the host, he swelled with pride, and in fierce tones said,— “Hearken, all ye demon troops, the host of heaven are my enemies, nor dare to stand up in open fight, but flee away at the sight of my greatarmy. There is one way of effecting their death, which I will declare; now listen to it. Go ye and put a stop to all feasting of Brahmans, to every sacrifice, oblation and funeral rite;
The forthwith the faint and hungry gods will come out to meet me, and whether I slay them or let them go, they will be equally in my power.”:

sections.label: Doha 182
sections.name: भुजबल बिस्व बस्य करि राखेसि कोउ न सुतंत्र

verses.sa:
मेघनाद कहुँ पुनि हँकरावा ।
दीन्ही सिख बलु बयरु बढ़ावा ॥
verses.tr:
meghanād kahum̐ puni ham̐karāvā
dīnhī sikh balu bayaru bar̤hāvā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
जे सुर समर धीर बलवाना ।
जिन्ह कें लरिबे कर अभिमाना ॥
verses.tr:
je sur samar dhīr balavānā
jinh keṃ laribe kar abhimānā

verses.sa:
तिन्हहि जीति रन आनेसु बाँधी ।
उठि सुत पितु अनुसासन काँधी ॥
verses.tr:
tinhahi jīti ran ānesu bām̐dhī
uṭhi sut pitu anusāsan kām̐dhī

verses.sa:
एहि बिधि सबही अग्या दीन्ही ।
आपुनु चलेउ गदा कर लीन्ही ॥
verses.tr:
ehi bidhi sabahī agyā dīnhī
āpunu caleu gadā kar līnhī

verses.sa:
चलत दसानन डोलति अवनी ।
गर्जत गर्भ स्त्रवहिं सुर रवनी ॥
verses.tr:
calat dasānan ḍolati avanī
garjat garbh stravahiṃ sur ravanī

verses.sa:
रावन आवत सुनेउ सकोहा ।
देवन्ह तके मेरु गिरि खोहा ॥
verses.tr:
rāvan āvat suneu sakohā
devanh take meru giri khohā

verses.sa:
दिगपालन्ह के लोक सुहाए ।
सूने सकल दसानन पाए ॥
verses.tr:
digapālanh ke lok suhāe
sūne sakal dasānan pāe

verses.sa:
पुनि पुनि सिंघनाद करि भारी ।
देइ देवतन्ह गारि पचारी ॥
verses.tr:
puni puni siṃghanād kari bhārī
dei devatanh gāri pacārī

verses.sa:
रन मद मत्त फिरइ जग धावा ।
प्रतिभट खौजत कतहुँ न पावा ॥
verses.tr:
ran mad matt phirai jag dhāvā
pratibhaṭ khaujat katahum̐ na pāvā

verses.sa:
रबि ससि पवन बरुन धनधारी ।
अगिनि काल जम सब अधिकारी ॥
verses.tr:
rabi sasi pavan barun dhanadhārī
agini kāl jam sab adhikārī

verses.sa:
किंनर सिद्ध मनुज सुर नागा ।
हठि सबही के पंथहिं लागा ॥
verses.tr:
kiṃnar siddh manuj sur nāgā
haṭhi sabahī ke paṃthahiṃ lāgā

verses.sa:
ब्रह्मसृष्टि जहँ लगि तनुधारी ।
दसमुख बसबर्ती नर नारी ॥
verses.tr:
brahmasṛṣṭi jaham̐ lagi tanudhārī
dasamukh basabartī nar nārī

verses.sa:
आयसु करहिं सकल भयभीता ।
नवहिं आइ नित चरन बिनीता ॥
verses.tr:
āyasu karahiṃ sakal bhayabhītā
navahiṃ āi nit caran binītā

verses.sa:
भुजबल बिस्व बस्य करि राखेसि कोउ न सुतंत्र ।
मंडलीक मनि रावन राज करइ निज मंत्र ॥
verses.tr:
bhujabal bisv basya kari rākhesi kou na sutaṃtr
maṃḍalīk mani rāvan rāj karai nij maṃtr
verses.head: दोहा

verses.sa:
देव जच्छ गंधर्व नर किंनर नाग कुमारि ।
जीति बरीं निज बाहुबल बहु सुंदर बर नारि ॥
verses.tr:
dev jacch gaṃdharv nar kiṃnar nāg kumāri
jīti barīṃ nij bāhubal bahu suṃdar bar nāri

trans: Again he called for Meghnad and exhorted him to yet greater courage and resentment,—" The strong and warlike gods, who venture to confront you, you must vanquish and bring here in chains.” Up rose the son to perform his father’s commands. In this manner he ordered all, and himself sallied forth, clab in hand. As he marched the earth shook, the heaven thundered, and pains of premature labour overtook the pregnant spouses of the gods. The gods themselves, on hearing of Ravan’s wrathfal approach, sought the caves of Mount Meru. As he approached in turn each of the eight quarters of the globe, he found it deserted by its guardian. Again and again he shouted the challenge to battle and vehemently scoffed at the gods, and mad with lust of blood traversed the whole universe in search of a foeman, nor could anywhere discover one.

When Narad met him, he said with a smile,—‘ Saint, where are the gods? show them to me.” Narad was not pleased to hear of his villainy, and forthwith sent him to White land. When he crossed the ocean and arrived on the other side, he saw a company of women, and said to them,— ‘Go tell your husbands that the king of the demons is here; then I will conquer them in battle and take you away to my own home.” On hearing this speech an ancient dame waxed wroth and ran and seized him by the feet and threw him up into the air;then after going a long way scratching and clawing, she gave him a good shake and pitched him with great violence into the middle of the sea.
Senseless, but by the Brahman’s blessing still alive, he sank down into hell; then with a roar sprang up again all unhurt, with a soul unmoved either by joy or sorrow.

After taking and pillaging the Naga’s capital, the enemy of heaven passed on to Bali’s realm. When the Dwarf heard of Ravan’s coming and how he had scoffed at Narad the gods’ teacher, the lord infused his own strength into all the children playing in the streets, who ran and seized him and brought him into the town, while every man and woman in the place flocked to see the sight,—“ Where on earth can heaven have brought such a creature from, with its twenty arms and ten heads?” Though the guards bound him and vexed him sore, he would rather die than tell his name; in the Dwarf’s presence he was much confounded, and the Merciful then had him set at liberty. Off at once rushed the demon king without the least shame or hesitation,

Shameless, pitiless, and ever bent on mischief, the tenheaded miscreant thought to conquer Rama. Hearken, Bharadvaja; if God is wroth with a man, his diamonds turn to bits of glass that are not worth a cowry.

Where ever he found a stray god or Brahman he frightened him into payment of ransom, and this is the way he went on day and night, the black-hearted ruffian. Then in haste he came to Pampapur, the seat of the monkey-king Bali, and beheld the beautiful lake that would charm the soul even of the greatest saint, where the monkey-king sat absorbed in contemplation. He smiled to see the Tenheaded, and Ravan shouted in a fury,—‘You wretched, senseless, hypocritical ane, I no sooner heard your name then I came at once; have done with your cowardice and meet me in battle.
Unless you.can vanquish me in combat your meditations are vain,” said the demon king, gnashing his 320 teeth.

sections.label: Doha 183
sections.name: बरनि न जाइ अनीति घोर निसाचर जो करहिं

verses.sa:
इंद्रजीत सन जो कछु कहेऊ ।
सो सब जनु पहिलेहिं करि रहेऊ ॥
verses.tr:
iṃdrajīt san jo kachu kaheū
so sab janu pahilehiṃ kari raheū
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
प्रथमहिं जिन्ह कहुँ आयसु दीन्हा ।
तिन्ह कर चरित सुनहु जो कीन्हा ॥
verses.tr:
prathamahiṃ jinh kahum̐ āyasu dīnhā
tinh kar carit sunahu jo kīnhā

verses.sa:
देखत भीमरूप सब पापी ।
निसिचर निकर देव परितापी ॥
verses.tr:
dekhat bhīmarūp sab pāpī
nisicar nikar dev paritāpī

verses.sa:
करहि उपद्रव असुर निकाया ।
नाना रूप धरहिं करि माया ॥
verses.tr:
karahi upadrav asur nikāyā
nānā rūp dharahiṃ kari māyā

verses.sa:
जेहि बिधि होइ धर्म निर्मूला ।
सो सब करहिं बेद प्रतिकूला ॥
verses.tr:
jehi bidhi hoi dharm nirmūlā
so sab karahiṃ bed pratikūlā

verses.sa:
जेहिं जेहिं देस धेनु द्विज पावहिं ।
नगर गाउँ पुर आगि लगावहिं ॥
verses.tr:
jehiṃ jehiṃ des dhenu dvij pāvahiṃ
nagar gāum̐ pur āgi lagāvahiṃ

verses.sa:
सुभ आचरन कतहुँ नहिं होई ।
देव बिप्र गुरू मान न कोई ॥
verses.tr:
subh ācaran katahum̐ nahiṃ hoī
dev bipr gurū mān na koī

verses.sa:
नहिं हरिभगति जग्य तप ग्याना ।
सपनेहुँ सुनिअ न बेद पुराना ॥
verses.tr:
nahiṃ haribhagati jagya tap gyānā
sapanehum̐ sunia na bed purānā

verses.sa:
जप जोग बिरागा तप मख भागा श्रवन सुनइ दससीसा ।
आपुनु उठि धावइ रहै न पावइ धरि सब घालइ खीसा ॥
verses.tr:
jap jog birāgā tap makh bhāgā śravan sunai dasasīsā
āpunu uṭhi dhāvai rahai na pāvai dhari sab ghālai khīsā
verses.head: छंद

verses.sa:
अस भ्रष्ट अचारा भा संसारा धर्म सुनिअ नहि काना ।
तेहि बहुबिधि त्रासइ देस निकासइ जो कह बेद पुराना ॥
verses.tr:
as bhraṣṭ acārā bhā saṃsārā dharm sunia nahi kānā
tehi bahubidhi trāsai des nikāsai jo kah bed purānā

verses.sa:
बरनि न जाइ अनीति घोर निसाचर जो करहिं ।
हिंसा पर अति प्रीति तिन्ह के पापहि कवनि मिति ॥
verses.tr:
barani na jāi anīti ghor nisācar jo karahiṃ
hiṃsā par ati prīti tinh ke pāpahi kavani miti
verses.head: दोहा

trans: Said Bali,—“ Away, I want no fighting; be wise and take your ten heads home. Your valour, friend, is undisputed, for I hear of your victories all over the world.” But Bali’s reiterated advice had not the slightest effect; and at last the monkey-king sprang up ina rage and seized Ravan and nipped him tight under his arms, and then forgot all about him for the space of ten months. One day as he raised his hands to offer a libation to the sun, RAvan slipped out of his clutches and ran away. Next he went, being still without either shame or scruple, to where the thousandarmed Sahasrabhuj was sporting in the water.
Ocean was troubled at Ravan’s might: the court began to sink, and Sahasrabahnu cried ina rage,—‘ What rival of mine is here to-day? ’.
_ Then he went and saw where Ravan stood, by whose giant arms the water was agitated, Potent in artifice as in strength of limb, he with a loud cry seized the king of

Lanka and kept him tied up for some daysin his stable—a sight of wonder for his wives. He was ashamed to tell his name, though the wise king was ever asking, and Rambhe and her companions danced about him and set a lighted torch to each of his ten heads. The saint Pulastya came and set him free. Next he went and got cursed by Nala.
On the road he spied a most incomparably beautiful damsel, with sandal-wood and flowers and _ leaves in her hand, going to worship Tripurari.

sections.label: Doha 184
sections.name: धरनि धरहि मन धीर कह बिरंचि हरिपद सुमिरु

verses.sa:
बाढ़े खल बहु चोर जुआरा ।
जे लंपट परधन परदारा ॥
verses.tr:
bār̤he khal bahu cor juārā
je laṃpaṭ paradhan paradārā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
मानहिं मातु पिता नहिं देवा ।
साधुन्ह सन करवावहिं सेवा ॥
verses.tr:
mānahiṃ mātu pitā nahiṃ devā
sādhunh san karavāvahiṃ sevā

verses.sa:
जिन्ह के यह आचरन भवानी ।
ते जानेहु निसिचर सब प्रानी ॥
verses.tr:
jinh ke yah ācaran bhavānī
te jānehu nisicar sab prānī

verses.sa:
अतिसय देखि धर्म कै ग्लानी ।
परम सभीत धरा अकुलानी ॥
verses.tr:
atisaya dekhi dharm kai glānī
param sabhīt dharā akulānī

verses.sa:
गिरि सरि सिंधु भार नहिं मोही ।
जस मोहि गरुअ एक परद्रोही ॥
verses.tr:
giri sari siṃdhu bhār nahiṃ mohī
jas mohi garua ek paradrohī

verses.sa:
सकल धर्म देखइ बिपरीता ।
कहि न सकइ रावन भय भीता ॥
verses.tr:
sakal dharm dekhai biparītā
kahi na sakai rāvan bhaya bhītā

verses.sa:
धेनु रूप धरि हृदयँ बिचारी ।
गई तहाँ जहँ सुर मुनि झारी ॥
verses.tr:
dhenu rūp dhari hṛdayam̐ bicārī
gaī tahām̐ jaham̐ sur muni jhārī

verses.sa:
निज संताप सुनाएसि रोई ।
काहू तें कछु काज न होई ॥
verses.tr:
nij saṃtāp sunāesi roī
kāhū teṃ kachu kāj na hoī

verses.sa:
सुर मुनि गंधर्बा मिलि करि सर्बा गे बिरंचि के लोका ।
सँग गोतनुधारी भूमि बिचारी परम बिकल भय सोका ॥
verses.tr:
sur muni gaṃdharbā mili kari sarbā ge biraṃci ke lokā
sam̐g gotanudhārī bhūmi bicārī param bikal bhaya sokā
verses.head: छंद

verses.sa:
ब्रह्माँ सब जाना मन अनुमाना मोर कछू न बसाई ।
जा करि तैं दासी सो अबिनासी हमरेउ तोर सहाई ॥
verses.tr:
brahmām̐ sab jānā man anumānā mor kachū na basāī
jā kari taiṃ dāsī so abināsī hamareu tor sahāī

verses.sa:
धरनि धरहि मन धीर कह बिरंचि हरिपद सुमिरु ।
जानत जन की पीर प्रभु भंजिहि दारुन बिपति ॥
verses.tr:
dharani dharahi man dhīr kah biraṃci haripad sumiru
jānat jan kī pīr prabhu bhaṃjihi dārun bipati
verses.head: दोहा

trans: Urvasi was abashed at seeing him, but Ravan addressed her in gentle tones,—*‘Who are you lady, and where are you going?’ She was too much overcome with modesty to give him an answer, Being mad with lust, he took no heed, but seized her by the hand, though she was the wife of Kuver's son. When he recognized her, there came upon him remorse and repentance for the evil deedi, and much troubled at heart the king of Jianke returned to his capital. Urvasi went sadly to Alaka and told Nala-Kuvra. In great wrath he uttered this curse,—‘ May the race of Ravan perish.” The curse went to Lanka where Ravan was seated, and stood before him. He trembled with dismay at the sight.
Submitting to the curse, he thought within himself that he had never taken any tribute from the monks; so in a fury,

He sent four messengers to a holy man’s hermitage, who on seeing them forgot all about the Supreme Spirit and asked them of their welfare, saying,—‘ Tell me, is all well with Lanka’s king #’ “Reverend sir, all is well with him, and he wants your tribute-money.” On hearing this speech he was much alarmed, and forgetful of his vow began to think within himself,—‘It is ill going empty-handed toa court where justice is not, and where a pack of villains are banded together.’ So he gave them a jar, which he had filled with blood taken from his own body, and made it over to the messengers, saying, —“ Go tell the king, Dohd 194. If the jar is opened, death will come upon you and your family.” The messengers in haste took the jar to the king’s court at Lanka.

Ravan was pleased at the sight of the jar, and the Messengers then told him what the saint had said. On hearing the curse his heart burned within him, and he said,— ‘“‘ Take the jar away to the north and carefully put it in the ground where no one can find it.” They took it to Janak’s dominions and there buried it ina field. There Janak, preparing for a sacrifice, was driving a golden plough: the offspring of the saint’s blood sprang up out of the furrow and was carried off by Garur. Her blessed name was at first Janaki, but Narad afterwards came and directed that it should be Sita’, and explained all the circumstances as above related. The great saint then left; the messengers also returned to Lanka, and Lank4’s lord, though worsted in four places, still greatly troubled the gods.
(Here ends the interpolation).

The sun and moon; the wind; Varuna and Kuver; fire, time and death, and every divine power; Kinnars, saints, men, gods and serpents, all were turned out of their course. From one end of earth to the other every living creature, whether male or female, was made subject to Ravan. All in turn do his bidding and cronch suppliantly at his feet.

By his mighty arm he subdued the whole universe and left not a single soul independent, but acting on his own counsel exercised dominion over the whole round world. And many were the lovely dames he wedded after conquest, daughters of gods and Yakshas and Gandharvas and men and Kinnars and Nagas.

Whatever he told Indrajit to do was done in less time than it took to tell: bear now how the other chiefs acted to whom he gave orders. The whole demon crew, villainous at heart and foul of aspect, the torment of heaven, were ready for any outrage, disguising themselves by the assumption of various forms and acting in every way contrary to the Veda, in order to eradicate religion. Wherever they find a cow or a Brahman, they at once set fire to the city, town or village; pious observances are no longer anywhere in existence; no respect is paid either to scripture, or Brahman, or spiritual instractor; there is no faith in Hari, no sacrifice, no prayer, nor alms-giving, and no one would ever dream of listening either to Veda or Purana.
At ahint of prayer or of penance, of sacrifice, vigil or fast,
Not a moment’s rest, but he hied on its quest, with a vow it should be the Last.
The world was sunk in lawlessness; all holy sounds were banned;
To read a sacred text was death, or exile from the land. Sorathd 21. The fearful oppression that the demons wrought is
beyond description: bent on mischief, there was no limit to their evil—doing.

The wicked all throve; such as thieves and gamblers, and those who coveted their neighbour's wife or goods, those who honoured neither father and mother nor the gods, and those who exacted service of better men than themselves. For people who act in this way, Bhavani, resemble demons. Seeing the general persecution of religion, earth was terrorstricken and dismayed,—‘the weight of mountains, lakes and seas is nothing so heavy as this one tyrant.. She saw all faith perverted, and yet for fear of Ravan could say nothing. After some consideration she took the form of a cow and went to the spot where the gods and saints were gathered together, and with tears declared to them her distress. There was no help to be had from any one of them.
Gods and saints and heavenly minstrels, flocked they all to Brahma's throne; With them Earth, a horned heifer, making sad and piteous moan.
Pondered: Brahma: in his wisdom,—‘ All vain is help of mine,
But a lord immortal. is thy Lord, be he my help and thine.’
“Take courage, Earth,” said Brahma, “and remember Hari; the Lord knows the distress of his servants, and will put an end to this cruel oppression.”

sections.label: Doha 185
sections.name: सुनि बिरंचि मन हरष तन पुलकि नयन बह नीर

verses.sa:
बैठे सुर सब करहिं बिचारा ।
कहँ पाइअ प्रभु करिअ पुकारा ॥
verses.tr:
baiṭhe sur sab karahiṃ bicārā
kaham̐ pāia prabhu karia pukārā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
पुर बैकुंठ जान कह कोई ।
कोउ कह पयनिधि बस प्रभु सोई ॥
verses.tr:
pur baikuṃṭh jān kah koī
kou kah payanidhi bas prabhu soī

verses.sa:
जाके हृदयँ भगति जसि प्रीति ।
प्रभु तहँ प्रगट सदा तेहिं रीती ॥
verses.tr:
jāke hṛdayam̐ bhagati jasi prīti
prabhu taham̐ pragaṭ sadā tehiṃ rītī

verses.sa:
तेहि समाज गिरिजा मैं रहेऊँ ।
अवसर पाइ बचन एक कहेऊँ ॥
verses.tr:
tehi samāj girijā maiṃ raheūm̐
avasar pāi bacan ek kaheūm̐

verses.sa:
हरि ब्यापक सर्बत्र समाना ।
प्रेम तें प्रगट होहिं मैं जाना ॥
verses.tr:
hari byāpak sarbatr samānā
prem teṃ pragaṭ hohiṃ maiṃ jānā

verses.sa:
देस काल दिसि बिदिसिहु माहीं ।
कहहु सो कहाँ जहाँ प्रभु नाहीं ॥
verses.tr:
des kāl disi bidisihu māhīṃ
kahahu so kahām̐ jahām̐ prabhu nāhīṃ

verses.sa:
अग जगमय सब रहित बिरागी ।
प्रेम तें प्रभु प्रगटइ जिमि आगी ॥
verses.tr:
ag jagamaya sab rahit birāgī
prem teṃ prabhu pragaṭai jimi āgī

verses.sa:
मोर बचन सब के मन माना ।
साधु साधु करि ब्रह्म बखाना ॥
verses.tr:
mor bacan sab ke man mānā
sādhu sādhu kari brahm bakhānā

verses.sa:
सुनि बिरंचि मन हरष तन पुलकि नयन बह नीर ।
अस्तुति करत जोरि कर सावधान मतिधीर ॥
verses.tr:
suni biraṃci man haraṣ tan pulaki nayan bah nīr
astuti karat jori kar sāvadhān matidhīr
verses.head: दोहा

trans: All the gods sat in counsel Where can we find the Lord andmake ourcry to him Said one,—* We must go to Vaikunth’; said another,—‘ His home is in the ocean. Nay, this is the way of the Lord, he is ever manifest to a faithful and loving soul.’ Now, Girije, ] too was in the assembly and took occasion to say briefly,—“ Hari is omnipresent everywhere alike, but, as I well know, is revealed by love. Tell] me any place, time or quarter of the heaven where the Lord is not. Present in all creation, animate or inanimate, passionless and unbiased, he is revealed like fire by love.’ My words were approved by all, and Brahma exclaimed,— ‘Well said, well said.’
The Creator was glad at heart and thrilled with delight, while his eyes filled with tears, and clasping his immortal hands he thus composedly and deliberately chanted his praises:

sections.label: Doha 186
sections.name: जानि सभय सुरभूमि सुनि बचन समेत सनेह

verses.sa:
जय जय सुरनायक जन सुखदायक प्रनतपाल भगवंता ।
गो द्विज हितकारी जय असुरारी सिधुंसुता प्रिय कंता ॥
verses.tr:
jaya jaya suranāyak jan sukhadāyak pranatapāl bhagavaṃtā
go dvij hitakārī jaya asurārī sidhuṃsutā priya kaṃtā
verses.head: छंद

verses.sa:
पालन सुर धरनी अद्भुत करनी मरम न जानइ कोई ।
जो सहज कृपाला दीनदयाला करउ अनुग्रह सोई ॥
verses.tr:
pālan sur dharanī adbhut karanī maram na jānai koī
jo sahaj kṛpālā dīnadayālā karau anugrah soī

verses.sa:
जय जय अबिनासी सब घट बासी ब्यापक परमानंदा ।
अबिगत गोतीतं चरित पुनीतं मायारहित मुकुंदा ॥
verses.tr:
jaya jaya abināsī sab ghaṭ bāsī byāpak paramānaṃdā
abigat gotītaṃ carit punītaṃ māyārahit mukuṃdā

verses.sa:
जेहि लागि बिरागी अति अनुरागी बिगतमोह मुनिबृंदा ।
निसि बासर ध्यावहिं गुन गन गावहिं जयति सच्चिदानंदा ॥
verses.tr:
jehi lāgi birāgī ati anurāgī bigatamoh munibṛṃdā
nisi bāsar dhyāvahiṃ gun gan gāvahiṃ jayati saccidānaṃdā

verses.sa:
जेहिं सृष्टि उपाई त्रिबिध बनाई संग सहाय न दूजा ।
सो करउ अघारी चिंत हमारी जानिअ भगति न पूजा ॥
verses.tr:
jehiṃ sṛṣṭi upāī tribidh banāī saṃg sahāya na dūjā
so karau aghārī ciṃt hamārī jānia bhagati na pūjā

verses.sa:
जो भव भय भंजन मुनि मन रंजन गंजन बिपति बरूथा ।
मन बच क्रम बानी छाड़ि सयानी सरन सकल सुर जूथा ॥
verses.tr:
jo bhav bhaya bhaṃjan muni man raṃjan gaṃjan bipati barūthā
man bac kram bānī chār̤i sayānī saran sakal sur jūthā

verses.sa:
सारद श्रुति सेषा रिषय असेषा जा कहुँ कोउ नहि जाना ।
जेहि दीन पिआरे बेद पुकारे द्रवउ सो श्रीभगवाना ॥
verses.tr:
sārad śruti seṣā riṣaya aseṣā jā kahum̐ kou nahi jānā
jehi dīn piāre bed pukāre dravau so śrībhagavānā

verses.sa:
भव बारिधि मंदर सब बिधि सुंदर गुनमंदिर सुखपुंजा ।
मुनि सिद्ध सकल सुर परम भयातुर नमत नाथ पद कंजा ॥
verses.tr:
bhav bāridhi maṃdar sab bidhi suṃdar gunamaṃdir sukhapuṃjā
muni siddh sakal sur param bhayātur namat nāth pad kaṃjā

verses.sa:
जानि सभय सुरभूमि सुनि बचन समेत सनेह ।
गगनगिरा गंभीर भइ हरनि सोक संदेह ॥
verses.tr:
jāni sabhaya surabhūmi suni bacan samet saneh
gaganagirā gaṃbhīr bhai harani sok saṃdeh
verses.head: दोहा

trans: ‘To the King of heaven be all glory given, refuge of
creation in distress and care,
Priests and kine befriending, hell’s brief triumph end-
ing, best beloved of Lakshmi, Ocean’s daughter fair.
Heaven and earth’s upholder, who, than all men bolder,
dares to scan the secret of thy strange mysterious way
Ever kind and loving, humble souls approving, may
thy gracious favour reach now to me, I pray.
immortal, lord of blissfulness supreme,
Ever pure and holy, whom the Queen of Folly has no power to tangle in her world-deluding dream.
Glory, glory, glory theme of endless story, sung by saints and sages in an ecstasy of love.
Daily, nightly gazing on the sight amazing, source of every blessing, Hari, lord of heaven above.
Triune incarnation, who at earth’s creation, wert alone presiding, and other aid was none;
Though in prayer unable, and my faith unstable, O great sin-destroyer, hear our hapless moan.
Life’s alarms dispelling, all disasters quelling comfort of the faithful, be our succour now;
All the gods implore thee, falling low before thee, with unfeigned submission of body, souland vow.
Find the theme too spacious, only know thee gracious; hasten then to help us in our hour of wrong.
In all grace excelling, Beauty’s chosen dwelling, ark on life’s dark ocean, home of ul most sweet,
Gods and saints and sages, now this tempest rages, fly in consternation to clasp thy lotus feet.”
Beholding the alarm of the gods and Earth, and hearing this devout speech, a dread voice came from heaven that removed all their doubt and anxiety, —

sections.label: Doha 187
sections.name: निज लोकहि बिरंचि गे देवन्ह इहइ सिखाइ

verses.sa:
जनि डरपहु मुनि सिद्ध सुरेसा ।
तुम्हहि लागि धरिहउँ नर बेसा ॥
verses.tr:
jani ḍarapahu muni siddh suresā
tumhahi lāgi dharihaum̐ nar besā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
अंसन्ह सहित मनुज अवतारा ।
लेहउँ दिनकर बंस उदारा ॥
verses.tr:
aṃsanh sahit manuj avatārā
lehaum̐ dinakar baṃs udārā

verses.sa:
कस्यप अदिति महातप कीन्हा ।
तिन्ह कहुँ मैं पूरब बर दीन्हा ॥
verses.tr:
kasyap aditi mahātap kīnhā
tinh kahum̐ maiṃ pūrab bar dīnhā

verses.sa:
ते दसरथ कौसल्या रूपा ।
कोसलपुरीं प्रगट नरभूपा ॥
verses.tr:
te dasarath kausalyā rūpā
kosalapurīṃ pragaṭ narabhūpā

verses.sa:
तिन्ह के गृह अवतरिहउँ जाई ।
रघुकुल तिलक सो चारिउ भाई ॥
verses.tr:
tinh ke gṛh avatarihaum̐ jāī
raghukul tilak so cāriu bhāī

verses.sa:
नारद बचन सत्य सब करिहउँ ।
परम सक्ति समेत अवतरिहउँ ॥
verses.tr:
nārad bacan satya sab karihaum̐
param sakti samet avatarihaum̐

verses.sa:
हरिहउँ सकल भूमि गरुआई ।
निर्भय होहु देव समुदाई ॥
verses.tr:
harihaum̐ sakal bhūmi garuāī
nirbhaya hohu dev samudāī

verses.sa:
गगन ब्रह्मबानी सुनी काना ।
तुरत फिरे सुर हृदय जुड़ाना ॥
verses.tr:
gagan brahmabānī sunī kānā
turat phire sur hṛdaya jur̤ānā

verses.sa:
तब ब्रह्मा धरनिहि समुझावा ।
अभय भई भरोस जियँ आवा ॥
verses.tr:
tab brahmā dharanihi samujhāvā
abhaya bhaī bharos jiyam̐ āvā

verses.sa:
निज लोकहि बिरंचि गे देवन्ह इहइ सिखाइ ।
बानर तनु धरि धरि महि हरि पद सेवहु जाइ ॥
verses.tr:
nij lokahi biraṃci ge devanh ihai sikhāi
bānar tanu dhari dhari mahi hari pad sevahu jāi
verses.head: दोहा

trans: ‘“« Fear not, Indra and ye saints and sages; for your sake I am about to assume the form of a man, with every element of my divinity incarnate in the glorious Solar race. For the severe penance practiced by Kasyapa and Aditi I granted them the full boon they asked. In the form of Dasarath and Kausalya they shall take royal birth in the city of Kosala. In their house shall become incarnate the four brothers, the pride of the family of Raghu. I will fulfil all that Narad predicted, by myself descending from heaven with my eternal spouse, and will remove the whole of earth’s burden.” On hearing the heavenly voice in the air the gods turned and were consoled, and Brahma exhorted Mother Earth, who forgot her fears in hopefalness.
Then Brahma proceeded to his own realm after thus instructing the gods,—‘ Go and worship Hari upon earth in form as monkeys.”

sections.label: Doha 188
sections.name: कौसल्यादि नारि प्रिय सब आचरन पुनीत

verses.sa:
गए देव सब निज निज धामा ।
भूमि सहित मन कहुँ बिश्रामा ॥
verses.tr:
gae dev sab nij nij dhāmā
bhūmi sahit man kahum̐ biśrāmā
verses.head: चौपाई

verses.sa:
जो कछु आयसु ब्रह्माँ दीन्हा ।
हरषे देव बिलंब न कीन्हा ॥
verses.tr:
jo kachu āyasu brahmām̐ dīnhā
haraṣe dev bilaṃb na kīnhā

verses.sa:
बनचर देह धरि छिति माहीं ।
अतुलित बल प्रताप तिन्ह पाहीं ॥
verses.tr:
banacar deh dhari chiti māhīṃ
atulit bal pratāp tinh pāhīṃ

verses.sa:
गिरि तरु नख आयुध सब बीरा ।
हरि मारग चितवहिं मतिधीरा ॥
verses.tr:
giri taru nakh āyudh sab bīrā
hari mārag citavahiṃ matidhīrā

verses.sa:
गिरि कानन जहँ तहँ भरि पूरी ।
रहे निज निज अनीक रचि रूरी ॥
verses.tr:
giri kānan jaham̐ taham̐ bhari pūrī
rahe nij nij anīk raci rūrī

verses.sa:
यह सब रुचिर चरित मैं भाषा ।
अब सो सुनहु जो बीचहिं राखा ॥
verses.tr:
yah sab rucir carit maiṃ bhāṣā
ab so sunahu jo bīcahiṃ rākhā

verses.sa:
अवधपुरीं रघुकुलमनि राऊ ।
बेद बिदित तेहि दसरथ नाऊँ ॥
verses.tr:
avadhapurīṃ raghukulamani rāū
bed bidit tehi dasarath nāūm̐

verses.sa:
धरम धुरंधर गुननिधि ग्यानी ।
हृदयँ भगति मति सारँगपानी ॥
verses.tr:
dharam dhuraṃdhar gunanidhi gyānī
hṛdayam̐ bhagati mati sāram̐gapānī

verses.sa:
कौसल्यादि नारि प्रिय सब आचरन पुनीत ।
पति अनुकूल प्रेम दृढ़ हरि पद कमल बिनीत ॥
verses.tr:
kausalyādi nāri priya sab ācaran punīt
pati anukūl prem dṛr̤h hari pad kamal binīt
verses.head: दोहा

trans: The gods went every one to his own abode, and with Earth had rest. All the orders that Brahma had given they executed gladly and without delay, Taking birth on earth as monkeys of incomparable strength and dignity, warriors with rocks and trees and claws for weapons, they confidently awaited Hari’s coming, swarming in every mountain and forest and divided among themselves into orderly troops, I have told you of their noble acts, and now you must hear of what was doing meanwhile elsewhere.
